title.zh: 卷一百二十三 列傳第十一 陳友諒 張士誠 方國珍 明玉珍
title.en: Volume 123 Biographies 11: Chen Youliang, Zhang Shicheng, Fang Guozhen, Ming Yuzhen
title.raw: 卷一百二十三 列傳第十一 陳友諒 張士誠 方國珍 明玉珍 Volume 123 Biographies 11: Chen Youliang, Zhang Shicheng, Fang Guozhen, Ming Yuzhen

sentences.zh: 陳友諒 張士誠 方國珍 明玉珍

translations.literal: Chen Youliang, Zhang Shicheng, Fang Guozhen, Ming Yuzhen
translations.idiomatic: Chen Youliang, Zhang Shicheng, Fang Guozhen, and Ming Yuzhen

sentences.zh: 陳友諒

translations.literal: Chen Youliang
translations.idiomatic: Chen Youliang

sentences.zh: 陳友諒，沔陽漁家子也。

translations.literal: Chen Youliang was a son of a fishing family in Mianyang.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Youliang was born into a fishing family in Mianyang.

sentences.zh: 本謝氏，祖贅于陳，因從其姓。

translations.literal: His original surname was Xie; his grandfather married into the Chen family and therefore took that surname.
translations.idiomatic: His family name had originally been Xie; a grandfather married into the Chen clan and adopted their surname.

sentences.zh: 少讀書，略通文義。

translations.literal: In youth he studied books and had a slight grasp of literary meaning.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he received some schooling and gained a modest command of letters.

sentences.zh: 有術者相其先世墓地，曰「法當貴」，友諒心竊喜。

translations.literal: A diviner examined the graves of his forebears and said, "By the method he ought to become noble"; Youliang secretly rejoiced in his heart.
translations.idiomatic: A fortune-teller who inspected his family's ancestral graves declared that the geomantic signs foretold greatness, and Youliang quietly exulted.

sentences.zh: 嘗為縣小吏，非其好也。

translations.literal: He once served as a petty clerk in the county; it was not to his liking.
translations.idiomatic: He once held a minor post as a county clerk, but the work did not suit him.

sentences.zh: 徐壽輝兵起，友諒往從之，依其將倪文俊為簿掾。

translations.literal: When Xu Shouhui raised troops, Youliang went to follow him and, relying on his general Ni Wenjun, served as a clerical officer.
translations.idiomatic: When Xu Shouhui took up arms, Youliang joined his cause and entered the service of Ni Wenjun, one of Shouhui's generals, as a clerk.

sentences.zh: 壽輝，羅田人，又名真一，業販布。

translations.literal: Shouhui was a man of Luotian, also called Zhenyi, and his occupation was selling cloth.
translations.idiomatic: Shouhui came from Luotian; he was also known as Zhenyi and had made his living as a cloth merchant.

sentences.zh: 元末盜起，袁州僧彭瑩玉以妖術與麻城鄒普勝聚眾為亂，用紅巾為號，奇壽輝狀貌，遂推為主。

translations.literal: At the end of the Yuan, bandits rose; the monk Peng Yingyu of Yuanzhou, by demonic arts, together with Zou Pusheng of Macheng gathered a crowd to rebel, using the Red Scarves as their sign; finding Shouhui's appearance remarkable, they thereupon pushed him forward as leader.
translations.idiomatic: When lawlessness spread at the close of the Yuan, the Yuanzhou monk Peng Yingyu, practicing heterodox rites, joined with Zou Pusheng of Macheng to raise a rebel host under the banner of the Red Turbans. Struck by Shouhui's striking looks, they made him their chief.

sentences.zh: 至正十一年九月陷蘄水及黃州路，敗元威順王寬徹不花。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the eleventh year of Zhizheng they captured Qishui and Huangzhou Circuit and defeated the Yuan Prince of Weishun, Kuanchibuhua.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of Zhizheng 11 (1351) they seized Qishui and Huangzhou, defeating the Yuan Prince of Weishun, Kuanchibuhua.

sentences.zh: 遂即蘄水為都，稱皇帝，國號天完，建元治平，以普勝為太師。

translations.literal: Thereupon they made Qishui their capital, styled themselves emperor, took the state name Tianwan, established the era name Zhiping, and appointed Pusheng Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: They then established their capital at Qishui, proclaimed an emperor, adopted the state name Tianwan, inaugurated the era Zhiping, and named Pusheng Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 未幾，陷饒、信。

translations.literal: Before long they captured Rao and Xin.
translations.idiomatic: Before long they also took Rao and Xin prefectures.

sentences.zh: 明年分兵四出，連陷湖廣、江西諸郡縣。

translations.literal: The next year they divided troops and sent them out in four directions, in succession capturing the various prefectures and counties of Huguang and Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: The following year they dispatched armies in every direction and in rapid succession overran prefectures and counties throughout Huguang and Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 遂破昱嶺關，陷杭州。

translations.literal: Thereupon they broke through Yuling Pass and captured Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: They broke through Yuling Pass and took Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 別將趙普勝等陷太平諸路。

translations.literal: A separate force under Zhao Pusheng and others captured the various circuits of Taiping.
translations.idiomatic: Other columns under Zhao Pusheng and others seized the Taiping region.

sentences.zh: 勢大振。

translations.literal: Their power greatly revived.
translations.idiomatic: Their power swelled dramatically.

sentences.zh: 然無遠志，所得不能守。

translations.literal: Yet they had no far-reaching ambition, and what they gained they could not hold.
translations.idiomatic: Yet they lacked long-range vision and could not hold what they seized.

sentences.zh: 明年為元師所破，壽輝走免。

translations.literal: The next year they were broken by Yuan troops, and Shouhui fled and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Yuan forces routed them, and Shouhui barely escaped.

sentences.zh: 已而復熾，遷都漢陽，為其丞相倪文俊所制。

translations.literal: Before long they flourished again; they moved the capital to Hanyang and were controlled by their chancellor Ni Wenjun.
translations.idiomatic: They soon revived, moved the capital to Hanyang, and fell under the control of their chancellor Ni Wenjun.

sentences.zh: 十七年九月，文俊謀弑壽輝，不克，奔黃州。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the seventeenth year Wenjun plotted to assassinate Shouhui but did not succeed and fled to Huangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of year seventeen Wenjun attempted to murder Shouhui but failed and fled to Huangzhou.

sentences.zh: 時友諒隸文俊麾下，數有功，為領兵元帥。

translations.literal: At that time Youliang was subordinate under Wenjun, repeatedly had merit, and was made commanding general.
translations.idiomatic: Youliang then served under Wenjun, distinguished himself in repeated campaigns, and was made a field marshal.

sentences.zh: 遂乘釁殺文俊，並其兵，自稱宣慰使，尋稱平章政事。

translations.literal: Thereupon he seized the opportunity to kill Wenjun, absorbed his troops, styled himself Pacification Commissioner, and soon styled himself Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: He seized the moment to kill Wenjun, absorbed his army, styled himself Pacification Commissioner, and soon took the title of Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 明年，陷安慶，又破龍興、瑞州，分兵取邵武、吉安，而自以兵入撫州。

translations.literal: The next year he captured Anqing, again broke Longxing and Ruizhou, divided troops to take Shaowu and Ji'an, and himself led troops into Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he took Anqing, defeated the garrisons at Longxing and Ruizhou, sent detachments against Shaowu and Ji'an, and personally marched on Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 已，又破建昌、贛、汀、信、衢。

translations.literal: Thereafter he again broke Jianchang, Gan, Ting, Xin, and Qu.
translations.idiomatic: He went on to conquer Jianchang, Ganzhou, Tingzhou, Xinzhou, and Quzhou.

sentences.zh: 當是時，江以南惟友諒兵最強。

translations.literal: At that time, south of the Yangtze, only Youliang's troops were strongest.
translations.idiomatic: At that time no force south of the Yangtze rivaled Youliang's army in strength.

sentences.zh: 太祖之取太平也，與為鄰。

translations.literal: When the Founding Emperor took Taiping, they became neighbors.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founding Emperor seized Taiping, their territories lay side by side.

sentences.zh: 友諒陷元池州，太祖遣常遇春擊取之，由是數相攻擊。

translations.literal: Youliang captured the Yuan prefecture of Chizhou; the Founding Emperor sent Chang Yuchun to strike and take it back, and from this they repeatedly attacked one another.
translations.idiomatic: Youliang seized Chizhou from the Yuan; the Founding Emperor sent Chang Yuchun to recover it, and from then on the two sides clashed again and again.

sentences.zh: 趙普勝者，故驍將，號「雙刀趙」。

translations.literal: Zhao Pusheng was a former fierce general, called "Double-Saber Zhao."
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Pusheng had been a ferocious commander in earlier days and was known as "Twin-Saber Zhao."

sentences.zh: 初與俞通海等屯巢湖，同歸太祖，叛去歸壽輝。

translations.literal: At first, together with Yu Tonghai and others, he encamped at Chaohu Lake and together submitted to the Founding Emperor, then rebelled and left to join Shouhui.
translations.idiomatic: He had once camped with Yu Tonghai and others at Chaohu Lake and submitted to the Founding Emperor along with them, but later defected to Shouhui.

sentences.zh: 至是為友諒守安慶，數引兵爭池州、太平，往來掠境上。

translations.literal: By this time he was holding Anqing for Youliang, repeatedly leading troops to contest Chizhou and Taiping, and coming and going to plunder the borderlands.
translations.idiomatic: Now he held Anqing for Youliang and repeatedly led raids to wrest Chizhou and Taiping from Ming control, harrying the frontier without cease.

sentences.zh: 太祖患之，啖普勝客，使潛入友諒軍間普勝。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor was troubled by this; he bribed Pusheng's guest and had him secretly enter Youliang's army to sow discord regarding Pusheng.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor, vexed by these incursions, won over one of Pusheng's retainers and sent him into Youliang's camp to breed suspicion between the two men.

sentences.zh: 普勝不之覺，見友諒使者輒訴功，悻悻有德色。

translations.literal: Pusheng did not perceive it; whenever he saw Youliang's envoys he would complain of his achievements, resentfully wearing a look of merit owed.
translations.idiomatic: Pusheng noticed nothing amiss; whenever Youliang's messengers appeared he boasted of his exploits with an air of injured pride, as though his due had been withheld.

sentences.zh: 友諒銜之，疑其貳於己，以會師為名，自江州猝至。

translations.literal: Youliang harbored resentment toward him, suspected that he was disloyal to himself, and under the pretext of joining forces suddenly arrived from Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Youliang took offense and suspected treachery; claiming he was coming to join forces, he rushed down from Jiangzhou without warning.

sentences.zh: 普勝以燒羊逆於雁漢。

translations.literal: Pusheng welcomed him with roast lamb at Yanhan.
translations.idiomatic: Pusheng went out to Yanhan to greet him with a feast of roast lamb.

sentences.zh: 甫登舟，友諒即殺普勝，並其軍。

translations.literal: As soon as he boarded the boat, Youliang at once killed Pusheng and absorbed his army.
translations.idiomatic: The moment Pusheng stepped aboard, Youliang killed him and absorbed his troops.

sentences.zh: 乃以輕兵襲池州，為徐達等擊敗，師盡覆。

translations.literal: Thereupon with light troops he raided Chizhou, was defeated by Xu Da and others, and his army was completely overthrown.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent a light force against Chizhou, but Xu Da and others routed it and destroyed the entire column.

sentences.zh: 始友諒破龍興，壽輝欲徙都之，友諒不可。

translations.literal: At first, when Youliang broke Longxing, Shouhui wished to move the capital there, but Youliang would not allow it.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after Youliang captured Longxing, Shouhui had wanted to move the capital there, but Youliang refused.

sentences.zh: 未幾，壽輝遽發漢陽，次江州。

translations.literal: Before long Shouhui suddenly set out from Hanyang and halted at Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Shouhui abruptly left Hanyang and made for Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 江州，友諒治所也，伏兵郭外，迎壽輝入，即閉城門，悉殺其所部。

translations.literal: Jiangzhou was Youliang's seat of government; he hid troops outside the walls, welcomed Shouhui in, then immediately closed the city gates and killed all of his followers.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangzhou was Youliang's base. He stationed men outside the walls, welcomed Shouhui inside, then shut the gates and slaughtered every soldier in Shouhui's train.

sentences.zh: 即江州為都，奉壽輝以居，而自稱漢王，置王府官屬。

translations.literal: He made Jiangzhou the capital, installed Shouhui to dwell there, and himself styled King of Han, establishing the officials of a princely establishment.
translations.idiomatic: He made Jiangzhou his capital, kept Shouhui there as a figurehead, and styled himself King of Han with a full princely court.

sentences.zh: 遂挾壽輝東下，攻太平。

translations.literal: Thereupon he took Shouhui eastward and attacked Taiping.
translations.idiomatic: He then marched east with Shouhui in tow and laid siege to Taiping.

sentences.zh: 太平城堅不可拔，乃引巨舟薄城西南。

translations.literal: Taiping's walls were strong and could not be taken; he therefore drew up huge ships close to the city's southwest.
translations.idiomatic: Taiping's walls proved too strong to storm, so he brought up great warships and pressed them against the southwest face of the city.

sentences.zh: 士卒緣舟尾攀堞而登，遂克之。

translations.literal: Soldiers climbed the battlements by scaling from the sterns of the boats and thus took it.
translations.idiomatic: His men swarmed up the battlements from the sterns of the ships and at last seized the city.

sentences.zh: 志益驕。

translations.literal: His ambition grew ever more arrogant.
translations.idiomatic: His arrogance only grew.

sentences.zh: 進駐採石磯，遣部將陽白事壽輝前，戒壯士挾鐵撾擊碎其首。

translations.literal: He advanced and encamped at Caishiji, sent a subordinate general Yang to report business before Shouhui, and instructed braves to strike and shatter his head with iron mallets.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced to Caishiji and sent a subordinate named Yang to present a report before Shouhui, with strongmen hidden nearby to crush his skull with iron mallets.

sentences.zh: 壽輝既死，以採石五通廟為行殿，即皇帝位，國號漢，改元大義，太師鄒普勝以下皆仍故官。

translations.literal: After Shouhui died, he took the Wutong Temple at Caishi as his traveling palace, ascended the imperial throne, took the state name Han, changed the era name to Dayi, and from Grand Preceptor Zou Pusheng downward all retained their former offices.
translations.idiomatic: Once Shouhui was dead, Youliang made the Wutong Temple at Caishi his provisional palace, proclaimed himself emperor, adopted the state name Han and the era Dayi, and left Zou Pusheng and the rest of the court in their former posts.

sentences.zh: 會大風雨，群臣班沙岸稱賀，不能成禮。

translations.literal: It happened that a great wind and rain arose; the ministers lined up on the sandy shore to offer congratulations but could not complete the rites.
translations.idiomatic: A violent storm broke out just then, and though his ministers arrayed themselves on the sandbank to offer congratulations, no proper ceremony could be completed.

sentences.zh: 友諒性雄猜，好以權術馭下。

translations.literal: Youliang's nature was bold and suspicious; he liked to control subordinates by stratagem and power.
translations.idiomatic: Youliang was bold, suspicious, and fond of ruling his followers through intrigue and manipulation.

sentences.zh: 既僭號，盡有江西、湖廣之地，恃其兵強，欲東取應天。

translations.literal: Having usurped the imperial title, he possessed all the lands of Jiangxi and Huguang, relied on the strength of his troops, and wished to seize Yingtian in the east.
translations.idiomatic: Once he had assumed an imperial title and held all of Jiangxi and Huguang, he trusted in his military strength and set his sights on conquering Yingtian in the east.

sentences.zh: 太祖患友諒與張士誠合，乃設計令其故人康茂才為書誘之，令速來。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor feared that Youliang would unite with Zhang Shicheng; he therefore devised a plan and had his old acquaintance Kang Maocai write a letter to lure him, ordering him to come quickly.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing an alliance between Youliang and Zhang Shicheng, the Founding Emperor arranged for his old comrade Kang Maocai to write a letter luring Youliang east with a promise of swift joint action.

sentences.zh: 友諒果引舟師東下，至江東橋，呼茂才不應，始知為所紿。

translations.literal: Youliang indeed led his fleet eastward; when he reached Jiangdong Bridge and called for Maocai, there was no answer, and he then knew he had been deceived.
translations.idiomatic: Youliang took the bait and sailed east with his fleet. At Jiangdong Bridge he called for Maocai and received no answer; only then did he realize he had been tricked.

sentences.zh: 戰于龍灣，大敗。

translations.literal: They fought at Longwan and he was greatly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Battle was joined at Longwan, and he suffered a crushing defeat.

sentences.zh: 潮落舟膠，死者無算，亡戰艦數百，乘輕舸走。

translations.literal: The tide fell and the boats stuck fast; the dead were beyond counting, several hundred warships were lost, and he fled in a light skiff.
translations.idiomatic: As the tide ebbed his ships ran aground; countless men perished and hundreds of warships were lost, and he escaped only in a light boat.

sentences.zh: 張德勝追敗之慈湖，焚其舟。

translations.literal: Zhang Desheng pursued and defeated him at Cihu and burned his boats.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Desheng pursued him to Cihu, defeated him again, and burned his fleet.

sentences.zh: 馮國勝以五翼軍蹙之，友諒出皁旗軍迎戰，又大敗。

translations.literal: Feng Guosheng pressed him with the Five-Wing Army; Youliang brought out his Black-Flag Army to meet the attack and was again greatly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Guosheng closed in with the Five-Wing Army; Youliang sent out his Black Banner corps to meet them and was routed once more.

sentences.zh: 遂棄太平，走江州。

translations.literal: Thereupon he abandoned Taiping and fled to Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He abandoned Taiping and fled back to Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 太祖兵乘勝取安慶，其將于光、歐普祥皆降。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor's army, riding the victory, took Anqing; his generals Yu Guang and Ou Puxiang both surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor's forces pressed their advantage, took Anqing, and received the surrender of Youliang's generals Yu Guang and Ou Puxiang.

sentences.zh: 明年，友諒遣兵復陷安慶。

translations.literal: The next year Youliang sent troops and again captured Anqing.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Youliang sent troops and recaptured Anqing.

sentences.zh: 太祖自將伐之，復安慶，長驅至江州。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor personally led a campaign against him, recovered Anqing, and drove in a long march to Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor led the campaign in person, retook Anqing, and marched straight on Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 友諒戰敗，夜挈妻子奔武昌。

translations.literal: Youliang was defeated in battle; by night he took his wife and children and fled to Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: Defeated in battle, Youliang fled by night to Wuchang with his wife and children.

sentences.zh: 其將吳宏以饒降，王溥以建昌降，胡廷瑞以龍興降。

translations.literal: His generals Wu Hong surrendered Rao, Wang Pu surrendered Jianchang, and Hu Tingrui surrendered Longxing.
translations.idiomatic: His generals defected one after another: Wu Hong surrendered Rao prefecture, Wang Pu Jianchang, and Hu Tingrui Longxing.

sentences.zh: 友諒忿疆土日蹙，乃大治樓船數百艘，皆高數丈，飾以丹漆，每船三重，置走馬棚，上下人語聲不相聞，艫箱皆裹以鐵。

translations.literal: Youliang, resentful that his territory daily shrank, thereupon greatly built several hundred tower-ships, all several zhang in height, adorned with cinnabar lacquer; each ship had three decks, with running-horse galleries set up; voices above and below could not hear one another, and the hulls were all wrapped in iron.
translations.idiomatic: Smarting as his domain shrank day by day, Youliang built several hundred tower ships, each several zhang tall and painted bright red. Every vessel had three decks with running galleries so that men on different levels could not hear one another's speech, and the hulls were sheathed in iron.

sentences.zh: 載家屬百官，盡銳攻南昌，飛梯沖車，百道並進。

translations.literal: Carrying his household and the hundred officials, with all his elite forces he attacked Nanchang; scaling ladders and battering rams advanced along a hundred routes at once.
translations.idiomatic: He embarked with his family and entire court, threw his best troops against Nanchang, and assaulted the walls simultaneously from a hundred directions with scaling ladders and battering rams.

sentences.zh: 太祖從子文正及鄧愈堅守，三月不能下，太祖自將救之。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor's nephew Wen Zheng and Deng Yu held firm; for three months it could not be taken, and the Founding Emperor personally led troops to relieve it.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor's nephew Zhu Wen Zheng and Deng Yu held the city stubbornly. After three months it still had not fallen, and the Founding Emperor marched to its relief in person.

sentences.zh: 友諒聞太祖至，撤圍，東出鄱陽湖，遇于康郎山。

translations.literal: When Youliang heard that the Founding Emperor had arrived, he lifted the siege, went east out onto Poyang Lake, and met him at Kanglang Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that the Founding Emperor was approaching, Youliang raised the siege, sailed east onto Poyang Lake, and encountered the Ming fleet at Kanglang Mountain.

sentences.zh: 友諒集巨艦，連鎖為陣，太祖兵不能仰攻，連戰三日，幾殆。

translations.literal: Youliang gathered huge ships and chained them into formation; the Founding Emperor's troops could not attack upward, and after three days of continuous fighting they were nearly destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Youliang massed his great ships and chained them into a battle line. The Ming forces could not strike upward against such heights, and after three days of fighting they were nearly undone.

sentences.zh: 已，東北風起，乃縱火焚友諒舟，其弟友仁等皆燒死。

translations.literal: Thereafter a northeast wind arose; they then set fire and burned Youliang's boats, and his younger brother Youren and others were all burned to death.
translations.idiomatic: Then a northeast wind sprang up, and the Ming set fire to Youliang's fleet. His brother Youren and many others perished in the flames.

sentences.zh: 友仁號五王，眇一目，有勇略，既死，友諒氣沮。

translations.literal: Youren was called the Fifth King; he had one blind eye and possessed courage and strategy; once he died, Youliang's spirit was broken.
translations.idiomatic: Youren, known as the Fifth King, was one-eyed but bold and resourceful. When he died, Youliang's morale collapsed.

sentences.zh: 是戰也，太祖舟雖小，然輕駛，友諒軍俱艨艟巨艦，不利進退，以是敗。

translations.literal: In this battle, although the Founding Emperor's boats were small, they were light and swift; Youliang's army all had covered war-junks and huge ships, ill-suited for advance and retreat, and for this reason was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: In this battle the Founding Emperor's vessels were small but nimble, whereas Youliang's force consisted entirely of heavy tower ships that could neither advance nor retreat readily, and for that reason he lost.

sentences.zh: 太祖所乘舟檣白，友諒約軍士明日並力攻白檣舟。

translations.literal: The mast of the boat the Founding Emperor rode was white; Youliang ordered his soldiers that on the morrow they should together attack the white-masted boat.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor's flagship had a white mast. Youliang ordered his men to concentrate the next day's attack on that white-masted vessel.

sentences.zh: 太祖知之，令舟檣盡白。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor learned of it and ordered that all boat masts be painted white.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founding Emperor learned of the plan, he ordered every mast in his fleet painted white.

sentences.zh: 翌日復戰，自辰至午，友諒軍大敗。

translations.literal: The next day they fought again; from the chen hour to the wu hour Youliang's army was greatly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: They fought again the next day from morning until noon, and Youliang's army was routed.

sentences.zh: 友諒欲退保奚山，太祖已先扼湖口，邀其歸路。

translations.literal: Youliang wished to withdraw and hold Mount Zeng, but the Founding Emperor had already seized Hukou beforehand and blocked his route of return.
translations.idiomatic: Youliang tried to fall back to Mount Zeng, but the Founding Emperor had already seized Hukou and cut off his retreat.

sentences.zh: 持數日，友諒謀于眾。

translations.literal: After holding on for several days, Youliang consulted with the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: After several days of stalemate, Youliang sought counsel from his officers.

sentences.zh: 右金吾將軍曰：「出湖難，宜焚舟登陸，直趨湖南圖再舉。

translations.literal: The Right Golden Crow General said: "Leaving the lake will be difficult; we ought to burn the boats, go ashore, and strike straight for Hunan to plan another rising."
translations.idiomatic: The Right Golden Crow General said, "Breaking out of the lake will be hard. We should burn the fleet, go ashore, and march straight into Hunan to regroup for another campaign."

sentences.zh: 」左金吾將軍曰：「此示弱也，彼以步騎躡我，進退失所據，大事去矣。

translations.literal: The Left Golden Crow General said: "This shows weakness; they will pursue us with infantry and cavalry, we will lose our footing in advance and retreat, and the great affair will be gone."
translations.idiomatic: The Left Golden Crow General replied, "That would show weakness. The enemy would run us down with infantry and cavalry; stripped of our ships we would have nowhere to stand, and all would be lost."

sentences.zh: 」友諒不能決，既而曰：「右金吾言是也。

translations.literal: Youliang could not decide; afterward he said: "The Right Golden Crow General's words are correct."
translations.idiomatic: Youliang could not make up his mind, but finally declared, "The Right Golden Crow General is right."

sentences.zh: 」左金吾以言不用，舉所部來降。

translations.literal: The Left Golden Crow General, because his words were not adopted, led all his command to come over and surrender.
translations.idiomatic: The Left Golden Crow General, rebuffed, brought his entire command over to the Ming side.

sentences.zh: 右金吾知之，亦降。

translations.literal: The Right Golden Crow General, learning of it, also surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: When the Right Golden Crow General learned of this, he surrendered as well.

sentences.zh: 友諒益困。

translations.literal: Youliang was increasingly pressed.
translations.idiomatic: Youliang's plight grew desperate.

sentences.zh: 太祖凡再移友諒書，其略曰：「吾欲與公約從，各安一方，以俟天命。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor twice sent letters to Youliang; the gist said: "I wish to make a covenant with you, each securing one region, to await Heaven's mandate."
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor wrote to Youliang twice. The gist of his message was: "I wish to make a pact with you so that each of us may hold his own territory and await Heaven's mandate."

sentences.zh: 公失計，肆毒於我。

translations.literal: "You misjudged and wantonly inflicted harm on me."
translations.idiomatic: "You chose wrongly and unleashed ruin upon me."

sentences.zh: 我輕師間出，奄有公龍興十一郡，猶不自悔禍，復構兵端。

translations.literal: "I sent a light force out by a side route and suddenly possessed your eleven commanderies of Longxing, yet you still did not repent your calamity and again raised the banner of war."
translations.idiomatic: "I marched a light force by a surprise route and seized your eleven Longxing prefectures, yet you still would not repent and again took up arms."

sentences.zh: 一困于洪都，再敗于康郎，骨肉將士重罹塗炭。

translations.literal: "Once trapped at Hongdu, twice defeated at Kanglang—kinsmen, generals, and soldiers repeatedly suffered ravage and ruin."
translations.idiomatic: "You were trapped once at Hongdu and defeated twice at Kanglang; your kin, your commanders, and your soldiers have again and again been cast into misery."

sentences.zh: 公即幸生還，亦宜卻帝號，坐待真主，不則喪家滅姓，悔晚矣。

translations.literal: "Even if you should by good fortune return alive, you ought still to set aside the imperial title and sit awaiting the true lord; otherwise you will lose house and extinguish clan, and regret will come too late."
translations.idiomatic: "Even if you should by some fortune escape alive, you ought to renounce your imperial title and wait quietly for the true sovereign. Otherwise you will lose your house and your name, and regret will come too late."

sentences.zh: 」友諒得書忿恚，不報。

translations.literal: Youliang, receiving the letter, was furious and did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Youliang read the letter in a fury and sent no answer.

sentences.zh: 久之乏食，突圍出湖口。

translations.literal: After a long time food ran short, and he broke through the encirclement and went out by Hukou.
translations.idiomatic: After a long siege his supplies gave out, and he forced a breakout toward Hukou.

sentences.zh: 諸將自上流邀擊之，大戰涇江口。

translations.literal: The generals intercepted and struck him from upstream; a great battle was fought at the mouth of the Jing River.
translations.idiomatic: Ming generals intercepted him from upstream, and a great battle was fought at the mouth of the Jing River.

sentences.zh: 漢軍且鬥且走，日暮猶不解。

translations.literal: The Han army fought as it fled; at dusk they still would not break off.
translations.idiomatic: The Han forces fought as they retreated, and even at dusk the battle had not ended.

sentences.zh: 友諒從舟中引首出，有所指捴，驟中流矢，貫晴及顱死。

translations.literal: Youliang stretched his head out from the boat, gesturing to direct something, when suddenly a stray arrow struck him, piercing his eye and skull so that he died.
translations.idiomatic: Youliang leaned out of his boat to give some command when suddenly a stray arrow struck him, piercing his eye and skull and killing him outright.

sentences.zh: 軍大潰，太子善兒被執。

translations.literal: The army collapsed in great disorder; the crown prince Shan'er was captured.
translations.idiomatic: His army collapsed in rout, and his crown prince Shan'er was taken prisoner.

sentences.zh: 太尉張定邊夜挾友諒次子理，載其屍遁還武昌。

translations.literal: Grand Marshal Zhang Dingbian by night took Youliang's second son Li, loaded his corpse, and fled back to Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: By night Grand Marshal Zhang Dingbian took Youliang's second son Li, placed the body aboard a boat, and fled back to Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 友諒豪侈，嘗造鏤金床甚工，宮中器物類是。

translations.literal: Youliang was extravagant; he once made a gold-inlaid bed of great craftsmanship, and the objects in the palace were of the same sort.
translations.idiomatic: Youliang had lived in lavish style; he once commissioned an exquisitely wrought gold-inlaid bed, and the furnishings of his palace were all of that kind.

sentences.zh: 既亡，江西行省以床進。

translations.literal: After he perished, the Jiangxi Branch Secretariat presented the bed.
translations.idiomatic: After his fall the Jiangxi provincial administration presented the bed to the court.

sentences.zh: 太祖歎曰：「此與孟昶七寶溺器何異！

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor sighed and said: "How is this different from Meng Chang's seven-treasure chamber pot!"
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor sighed and said, "How is this different from Meng Chang's jeweled chamber pot!"

sentences.zh: 」命有司毀之。

translations.literal: He ordered the relevant offices to destroy it.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the authorities to destroy it.

sentences.zh: 友諒僭號凡四年。

translations.literal: Youliang's usurped title lasted altogether four years.
translations.idiomatic: Youliang had held his usurped imperial title for four years in all.

sentences.zh: 子理既還武昌，嗣偽位，改元德壽。

translations.literal: His son Li, having returned to Wuchang, succeeded to the false throne and changed the era name to Deshou.
translations.idiomatic: His son Li, once back in Wuchang, succeeded to the rebel throne and proclaimed the era Deshou.

sentences.zh: 是冬，太祖親征武昌。

translations.literal: That winter the Founding Emperor personally campaigned against Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: That winter the Founding Emperor led a personal campaign against Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 明年二月再親征。

translations.literal: The next year in the second month he again personally campaigned.
translations.idiomatic: The following February he led another personal campaign.

sentences.zh: 其丞相張必先自岳州來援，次洪山。

translations.literal: His chancellor Zhang Bixian came from Yuezhou to relieve him and halted at Hongshan.
translations.idiomatic: His chancellor Zhang Bixian marched from Yuezhou to relieve the city and encamped at Hongshan.

sentences.zh: 常遇春擊擒之，徇於城下。

translations.literal: Chang Yuchun struck, captured him, and paraded him beneath the walls.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Yuchun defeated and captured him, then paraded him before the walls of Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 必先，驍將也，軍中號「潑張」，倚為重。

translations.literal: Bixian was a fierce general; in the army he was called "Wild Zhang," and they relied on him as a mainstay.
translations.idiomatic: Bixian was a formidable commander known in camp as "Wild Zhang," and the Han army had leaned heavily on him.

sentences.zh: 及被擒，城中大懼，由是欲降者眾。

translations.literal: When he was captured, the city was greatly afraid, and from this many wished to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Once he was taken, panic spread through the city and many began to urge surrender.

sentences.zh: 太祖乃遣其故臣羅復仁入城招理。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor thereupon sent his former subject Luo Furen into the city to summon Li.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor then sent his former follower Luo Furen into the city to negotiate Li's surrender.

sentences.zh: 理遂降，入軍門，俯伏不敢視。

translations.literal: Li thereupon surrendered; entering the army gate, he prostrated himself and dared not look up.
translations.idiomatic: Li surrendered, entered the camp gate, and prostrated himself without daring to raise his eyes.

sentences.zh: 太祖見理幼弱，掖之起，握其手曰：「吾不汝罪也。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor, seeing Li was young and weak, helped him rise, grasped his hand, and said: "I will not punish you."
translations.idiomatic: Seeing how young and frail Li was, the Founding Emperor helped him to his feet, took his hand, and said, "I will not hold this against you."

sentences.zh: 」府庫財物恣理取，旋應天，授爵歸德侯。

translations.literal: He allowed Li to take freely from the treasury stores and goods, then soon went to Yingtian and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Guide.
translations.idiomatic: He let Li take whatever he wished from the treasury, then brought him to Yingtian and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Guide.

sentences.zh: 友諒之從徐壽輝也，其父普才止之。

translations.literal: When Youliang followed Xu Shouhui, his father Pucai tried to stop him.
translations.idiomatic: When Youliang joined Xu Shouhui's cause, his father Pucai tried to dissuade him.

sentences.zh: 不聽。

translations.literal: He would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Youliang would not listen.

sentences.zh: 及貴，往迎之。

translations.literal: When he became noble, he went to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Once he had risen to power, Youliang went to bring his father to court.

sentences.zh: 普才曰：「汝違吾命，吾不知死所矣。

translations.literal: Pucai said: "You disobeyed my command; I do not know where I shall die."
translations.idiomatic: Pucai said, "You defied my wishes. I no longer know where I am to die."

sentences.zh: 」普才五子：長友富，次友直，又次友諒，又次友仁、友貴。

translations.literal: Pucai had five sons: the eldest Youfu, next Youzhi, then Youliang, then Youren and Yougui.
translations.idiomatic: Pucai had five sons: Youfu, Youzhi, Youliang, Youren, and Yougui, in that order.

sentences.zh: 友仁、友貴前死鄱陽。

translations.literal: Youren and Yougui had earlier died at Poyang.
translations.idiomatic: Youren and Yougui had already died at Poyang.

sentences.zh: 太祖平武昌，封普才承恩侯，友富歸仁伯，友直懷恩伯，贈友仁康山王，命所司立廟祀之，以友貴祔。

translations.literal: When the Founding Emperor pacified Wuchang, he enfeoffed Pucai as Marquis of Chengen, Youfu as Earl of Guiren, and Youzhi as Earl of Huai'en; he posthumously ennobled Youren as Prince of Kangshan, ordered the relevant offices to erect a temple to sacrifice to him, and had Yougui enshrined alongside.
translations.idiomatic: After pacifying Wuchang, the Founding Emperor enfeoffed Pucai as Marquis of Chengen, Youfu as Earl of Guiren, and Youzhi as Earl of Huai'en; he posthumously created Youren Prince of Kangshan, ordered a temple built in his honor, and had Yougui enshrined beside him.

sentences.zh: 理居京師，邑邑出怨望語。

translations.literal: Li dwelt in the capital and from time to time uttered words of resentment and discontent.
translations.idiomatic: While living in the capital, Li occasionally let slip resentful and disloyal remarks.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「此童孺小過耳，恐細人蠱惑，不克全朕恩，宜處之遠方。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "This is merely a child's small fault, but I fear petty men may bewitch and delude him so that my grace cannot be fully preserved; he ought to be placed in a distant region."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "These are only the indiscretions of a boy, but I fear that schemers may turn his head and make it impossible for me to show him complete favor. He should be sent far away."

sentences.zh: 」洪武五年，理及歸義侯明升並徙高麗，遣元降臣樞密使延安答理護行。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Hongwu, Li and the Marquis of Guiyi Ming Sheng were both relocated to Goryeo, and the surrendered Yuan minister and Privy Council envoy Yan'an Dalai was sent to escort them.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 5 (1372), Li and the Marquis of Guiyi Ming Sheng were both exiled to Goryeo under the escort of the former Yuan Privy Council envoy Yan'an Dalai.

sentences.zh: 賜高麗王羅綺，俾善視之。

translations.literal: He bestowed silks on the King of Goryeo and ordered that they be well cared for.
translations.idiomatic: He sent silks as gifts to the King of Goryeo and instructed him to treat the exiles well.

sentences.zh: 亦徙普才等滁陽。

translations.literal: He also relocated Pucai and the others to Chuyang.
translations.idiomatic: Pucai and the rest of the family were also moved to Chuyang.

sentences.zh: 熊天瑞者，本荊州樂工，從徐壽輝抄略江、湘間。

translations.literal: Xiong Tianrui was originally a musician of Jingzhou; he followed Xu Shouhui in raiding between the Yangtze and the Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong Tianrui had originally been a musician in Jingzhou. He followed Xu Shouhui in plundering the lands along the Yangtze and the Xiang.

sentences.zh: 後受陳友諒命，攻陷臨江、吉安，又陷贛州。

translations.literal: Later, receiving Chen Youliang's orders, he attacked and captured Linjiang and Ji'an, and again captured Ganzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Later, acting on Chen Youliang's orders, he seized Linjiang and Ji'an and then took Ganzhou.

sentences.zh: 友諒俾以參知政事，守贛，兼統吉安、南安、南雄、韶州諸路。

translations.literal: Youliang appointed him Vice Grand Councillor to hold Gan and concurrently command the circuits of Ji'an, Nan'an, Nanxiong, and Shaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Youliang made him Vice Grand Councillor and governor of Ganzhou, with authority over Ji'an, Nan'an, Nanxiong, and Shaozhou as well.

sentences.zh: 久之，陽言東下，署其幟曰「無敵」，自稱金紫光祿大夫、司徒、平章軍國重事。

translations.literal: After a long time he falsely claimed he was going east, inscribed his banners with the words "Invincible," and styled himself Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, Minister of Education, and Grand Councillor of Important State and Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he pretended to march east, emblazoned his banners with the word "Invincible," and took for himself the titles of Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, Minister of Education, and Grand Councillor of Important State and Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 友諒不能制。

translations.literal: Youliang could not control him.
translations.idiomatic: Youliang could not restrain him.

sentences.zh: 陰圖取廣東，造戰艦于南雄，帥數萬眾趨廣州。

translations.literal: Secretly he plotted to take Guangdong, built warships at Nanxiong, and led tens of thousands toward Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly planned to seize Guangdong, built warships at Nanxiong, and marched on Guangzhou at the head of tens of thousands of men.

sentences.zh: 元將何真以兵迎于胥江。

translations.literal: The Yuan general He Zhen met him with troops at Xujiang.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuan general He Zhen confronted him with an army at Xujiang.

sentences.zh: 會天大雷雨，震其艦檣折，天瑞懼而還。

translations.literal: It happened that a great thunderstorm arose; lightning broke his ship's mast, and Tianrui, afraid, returned.
translations.idiomatic: A violent thunderstorm struck, lightning shattered the mast of his flagship, and Tianrui turned back in fear.

sentences.zh: 太祖兵克臨江，遣常遇春等攻贛，天瑞拒守五越月，至正二十五年正月，乃帥其養子元震肉袒詣軍門降。

translations.literal: When the Founding Emperor's army captured Linjiang, he sent Chang Yuchun and others to attack Gan; Tianrui held out for more than five months, and in the first month of the twenty-fifth year of Zhizheng he led his adopted son Yuanzhen, bare-chested, to the army gate to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: After Ming forces took Linjiang, the Founding Emperor sent Chang Yuchun against Ganzhou. Tianrui held out for more than five months, but in the first month of Zhizheng 25 (1365) he came to the camp bare-chested with his adopted son Yuanzhen and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 太祖宥之，授指揮使。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor pardoned him and appointed him a commander.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor spared his life and appointed him a military commander.

sentences.zh: 明年從攻浙西，叛降于張士誠，教士誠飛礮擊外軍。

translations.literal: The next year, while following the attack on western Zhejiang, he rebelled and surrendered to Zhang Shicheng, teaching Shicheng to use flying catapults to strike the besieging army.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, during the campaign in western Zhejiang, he defected to Zhang Shicheng and taught him how to use trebuchets against the besieging Ming army.

sentences.zh: 城中木石俱盡，外軍多傷者。

translations.literal: Timber and stones within the city were all exhausted, and many in the outside army were wounded.
translations.idiomatic: The city's timber and stone ammunition ran out, but many besiegers were killed or wounded.

sentences.zh: 士誠滅，天瑞伏誅。

translations.literal: When Shicheng was destroyed, Tianrui was executed.
translations.idiomatic: When Shicheng fell, Tianrui was put to death.

sentences.zh: 有周時中者，龍泉人，嘗為壽輝平章。

translations.literal: There was a Zhou Shizhong, a man of Longquan, who had once served Shouhui as Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Shizhong of Longquan had once served as Grand Councillor under Xu Shouhui.

sentences.zh: 後帥所部降，策天瑞必叛。

translations.literal: Later he led his command to surrender and predicted that Tianrui would surely rebel.
translations.idiomatic: He later surrendered with his troops and predicted that Tianrui would rebel.

sentences.zh: 後果如其言。

translations.literal: Afterward it indeed came about as he had said.
translations.idiomatic: Events proved him right.

sentences.zh: 時中累官吏部尚書，出為鎮江知府，曆福建鹽運副使。

translations.literal: Shizhong rose through offices to Minister of Personnel, went out as prefect of Zhenjiang, and served as deputy salt commissioner of Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhong rose to Minister of Personnel, served as prefect of Zhenjiang, and later as deputy salt commissioner of Fujian.

sentences.zh: 元震本姓田氏，善戰有名。

translations.literal: Yuanzhen's original surname was Tian; he was skilled in battle and had a reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhen had been born into the Tian clan and was renowned as a fighter.

sentences.zh: 遇春之圍贛也，元震竊出覘兵，遇春亦引數騎出，猝與遇。

translations.literal: When Yuchun was besieging Gan, Yuanzhen stole out to reconnoiter the troops; Yuchun also led out several horsemen, and they suddenly met.
translations.idiomatic: While Yuchun was besieging Ganzhou, Yuanzhen slipped out to scout the enemy lines. Yuchun too rode out with a few horsemen, and the two parties met by chance.

sentences.zh: 元震不知為遇春也，過之。

translations.literal: Yuanzhen did not know it was Yuchun and passed by.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhen did not recognize Yuchun and rode past.

sentences.zh: 及遇春還，始覺，遂單騎前襲遇春。

translations.literal: When Yuchun returned, he at last realized it and thereupon, alone on horseback, rode forward to attack Yuchun.
translations.idiomatic: Only after Yuchun had turned back did Yuanzhen realize who it was, and he wheeled around alone to charge him.

sentences.zh: 遇春遣從騎揮刀擊之，元震奮鐵撾且鬥且走。

translations.literal: Yuchun sent his attendant horsemen to slash at him with blades; Yuanzhen brandished an iron mallet, fighting as he fled.
translations.idiomatic: Yuchun's escorts slashed at him with their swords, but Yuanzhen fought them off with an iron mallet as he retreated.

sentences.zh: 遇春曰：「壯男子也。

translations.literal: Yuchun said: "A stalwart fellow."
translations.idiomatic: Yuchun said, "What a brave man."

sentences.zh: 」舍之。

translations.literal: He let him go.
translations.idiomatic: He let him go.

sentences.zh: 由是喜其才勇。

translations.literal: From this he delighted in his talent and courage.
translations.idiomatic: From that moment he admired the man's courage and skill.

sentences.zh: 既從天瑞降，薦以為指揮使。

translations.literal: After he followed Tianrui in surrendering, he was recommended and made a commander.
translations.idiomatic: After Yuanzhen surrendered with Tianrui, Yuchun recommended him for a commander's post.

sentences.zh: 天瑞誅，復故姓雲。

translations.literal: When Tianrui was executed, he restored his former surname Yun.
translations.idiomatic: When Tianrui was executed, he resumed his original surname, Yun.

sentences.zh: 張士誠

translations.literal: Zhang Shicheng
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shicheng

sentences.zh: 張士誠，小字九四，泰州白駒場亭人。

translations.literal: Zhang Shicheng, childhood name Jiusi, was a man of Baiting in Baiju Field, Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shicheng, whose childhood name was Jiusi, came from Baiting in Baiju Field, Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 有弟三人，並以操舟運鹽為業，緣私作奸利。

translations.literal: He had three younger brothers; all took pole-boats to transport salt as their occupation and, taking advantage of private opportunities, engaged in illicit profit.
translations.idiomatic: He had three younger brothers. Together they made their living hauling salt by boat and profited from smuggling on the side.

sentences.zh: 頗輕財好施，得群輩心。

translations.literal: He was rather free with wealth and fond of giving, and won the hearts of the crowd.
translations.idiomatic: He was generous with money and won the loyalty of his fellows.

sentences.zh: 常鬻鹽諸富家，富家多陵侮之，或負其直不酬。

translations.literal: He often sold salt to various wealthy families; the wealthy families mostly bullied and insulted him, or owed him the price and did not pay.
translations.idiomatic: He often sold salt to wealthy households, who bullied him and sometimes refused to pay what they owed.

sentences.zh: 而弓手丘義尤窘辱士誠甚。

translations.literal: Moreover the bowman Qiu Yi especially distressed and humiliated Shicheng.
translations.idiomatic: The bowman Qiu Yi humiliated him worse than any of the rest.

sentences.zh: 士誠忿，即帥諸弟及壯士李伯升等十八人殺義，並滅諸富家，縱火焚其居。

translations.literal: Shicheng was angry; he immediately led his brothers and the stalwart Li Bosheng and seventeen others to kill Yi, and together destroyed the wealthy families and set fire to burn their dwellings.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Shicheng gathered his brothers and seventeen stalwarts including Li Bosheng, killed Qiu Yi, slaughtered the wealthy families who had wronged him, and burned their houses.

sentences.zh: 入旁郡場，招少年起兵。

translations.literal: He entered a neighboring district salt field, recruited youths, and raised troops.
translations.idiomatic: He crossed into a neighboring salt district, rallied young men, and raised an army.

sentences.zh: 鹽丁方苦重役，遂共推為主，陷泰州。

translations.literal: The salt laborers were then suffering under heavy corvée, and together they pushed him forward as leader and captured Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Salt workers groaning under heavy labor duties made him their leader and together they seized Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 高郵守李齊諭降之，復叛。

translations.literal: Li Qi, defender of Gaoyou, instructed him to surrender, but he rebelled again.
translations.idiomatic: Li Qi, the Gaoyou commander, persuaded him to submit, but he rebelled again.

sentences.zh: 殺行省參政趙璉，並陷興化，結砦德勝湖，有眾萬餘。

translations.literal: He killed the Branch Secretariat Vice Commissioner Zhao Lian, also captured Xinghua, established a stockade at Desheng Lake, and had more than ten thousand followers.
translations.idiomatic: He killed the Branch Secretariat Vice Commissioner Zhao Lian, took Xinghua as well, fortified a camp at Desheng Lake, and gathered more than ten thousand men.

sentences.zh: 元以萬戶告身招之。

translations.literal: The Yuan used a ten-thousand-household appointment document to recruit him.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuan court offered him a ten-thousand-household commission to win him over.

sentences.zh: 不受。

translations.literal: He did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He refused.

sentences.zh: 紿殺李齊，襲據高郵，自稱誠王，僭號大周，建元天祐。

translations.literal: He deceived and killed Li Qi, seized Gaoyou by surprise, styled himself King of Cheng, usurped the title of Great Zhou, and established the era name Tianyou.
translations.idiomatic: He tricked and killed Li Qi, seized Gaoyou, styled himself King of Cheng, proclaimed the state of Great Zhou, and adopted the era name Tianyou.

sentences.zh: 是歲至正十三年也。

translations.literal: That year was the thirteenth year of Zhizheng.
translations.idiomatic: This was Zhizheng 13 (1353).

sentences.zh: 明年，元右丞相脫脫總大軍出討，數敗士誠，圍高郵，隳其外城。

translations.literal: The next year the Yuan Right Chancellor Toghto commanded a great army to campaign against him, repeatedly defeated Shicheng, besieged Gaoyou, and destroyed its outer wall.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the Yuan Right Chancellor Toghto led a great army against him, defeated him repeatedly, besieged Gaoyou, and breached its outer walls.

sentences.zh: 城且下，順帝信讒，解脫脫兵柄，削官爵，以他將代之。

translations.literal: The city was about to fall when the Shundi Emperor believed slander, removed Toghto from military authority, stripped his titles, and replaced him with another general.
translations.idiomatic: Just as the city was about to fall, the Shundi Emperor believed slander against Toghto, stripped him of command and rank, and replaced him with another general.

sentences.zh: 士誠乘間奮擊，元兵潰去，由是復振。

translations.literal: Shicheng seized the interval and struck fiercely; the Yuan troops collapsed and fled, and from this he revived again.
translations.idiomatic: Shicheng seized the moment and counterattacked fiercely. The Yuan army broke and fled, and his fortunes revived.

sentences.zh: 逾年，淮東饑，士誠乃遣弟士德由通州渡江入常熟。

translations.literal: After a year the east Huai region suffered famine; Shicheng thereupon sent his younger brother Shide from Tongzhou to cross the river and enter Changshu.
translations.idiomatic: The following year famine struck eastern Huai, and Shicheng sent his brother Shide across the Yangtze from Tongzhou into Changshu.

sentences.zh: 十六年二月陷平江，並陷湖州、松江及常州諸路。

translations.literal: In the second month of the sixteenth year he captured Pingjiang and also captured the circuits of Huzhou, Songjiang, and Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of year sixteen he took Pingjiang along with Huzhou, Songjiang, and Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 改平江為隆平府，士誠自高郵來都之。

translations.literal: He changed Pingjiang to Long'an Prefecture, and Shicheng came from Gaoyou to make it his capital.
translations.idiomatic: He renamed Pingjiang Long'an Prefecture and moved his capital there from Gaoyou.

sentences.zh: 即承天寺為府第，踞坐大殿中，射三矢於棟以識。

translations.literal: He took Chengtian Temple as his prefectural residence, sat astride in the great hall, and shot three arrows into the ridgepole to mark it.
translations.idiomatic: He made Chengtian Temple his palace, seated himself in the main hall, and shot three arrows into a roof beam to mark the spot.

sentences.zh: 是歲，太祖亦下集慶，遣楊憲通好於士誠。

translations.literal: That year the Founding Emperor also took Jiqing and sent Yang Xian to open friendly relations with Shicheng.
translations.idiomatic: That same year the Founding Emperor seized Jiqing and sent Yang Xian to propose friendly relations with Shicheng.

sentences.zh: 其書曰：「昔隗囂稱雄於天水，今足下亦擅號于姑蘇，事勢相等，吾深為足下喜。

translations.literal: His letter said: "In old times Wei Xiao called himself hegemon at Tianshui; now you too hold a title alone at Gusu—the situations are equal, and I deeply rejoice for you."
translations.idiomatic: His letter read: "Long ago Wei Xiao made himself master of Tianshui; now you hold sway at Gusu. Our positions are much alike, and I congratulate you sincerely."

sentences.zh: 睦鄰守境，古人所貴，竊甚慕焉。

translations.literal: Keeping good relations with neighbors and guarding the borders are what the ancients prized; I privately greatly admire this.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients prized neighborly peace and secure borders, and I deeply admire your example.

sentences.zh: 自今信使往來，毋惑讒言，以生邊釁。

translations.literal: "From now on let envoys come and go; do not be misled by slanderous words to breed border strife."
translations.idiomatic: "Let our envoys pass freely hereafter, and do not let slander breed conflict between us."

sentences.zh: 」士誠得書，留憲不報。

translations.literal: Shicheng received the letter, detained Xian, and made no reply.
translations.idiomatic: Shicheng received the letter, detained Yang Xian, and sent no reply.

sentences.zh: 已，遣舟師攻鎮江。

translations.literal: Before long he sent a fleet to attack Zhenjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he sent his fleet against Zhenjiang.

sentences.zh: 徐達敗之于龍潭。

translations.literal: Xu Da defeated him at Longtan.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Da defeated him at Longtan.

sentences.zh: 太祖遣達及湯和攻常州。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor sent Da and Tang He to attack Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor sent Xu Da and Tang He against Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 士誠兵來援，大敗，失張、湯二將，乃以書求和，請歲輸粟二十萬石，黃金五百兩，白金三百斤。

translations.literal: Shicheng's troops came to relieve it and were greatly defeated; he lost the two generals Zhang and Tang, and thereupon sent a letter seeking peace, requesting to deliver annually two hundred thousand piculs of grain, five hundred taels of gold, and three hundred jin of white silver.
translations.idiomatic: Shicheng sent relief forces but suffered a crushing defeat and lost two generals named Zhang and Tang. He then sued for peace, offering two hundred thousand piculs of grain per year plus five hundred taels of gold and three hundred jin of silver.

sentences.zh: 太祖答書，責其歸楊憲，歲輸五十萬石。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor answered with a letter, reproaching him to return Yang Xian and demanding five hundred thousand piculs annually.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor replied, demanding the return of Yang Xian and raising the annual tribute to five hundred thousand piculs of grain.

sentences.zh: 士誠復不報。

translations.literal: Shicheng again made no reply.
translations.idiomatic: Shicheng again sent no answer.

sentences.zh: 初，士誠既得平江，即以兵攻嘉興。

translations.literal: At first, once Shicheng had obtained Pingjiang, he immediately sent troops to attack Jiaxing.
translations.idiomatic: Once Shicheng held Pingjiang, he immediately attacked Jiaxing.

sentences.zh: 元守將苗帥楊完者數敗其兵。

translations.literal: The Yuan defending general, the Miao commander Yang Wanzhe, repeatedly defeated his troops.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuan defender Yang Wanzhe, a Miao commander, defeated him again and again.

sentences.zh: 乃遣士德間道破杭州。

translations.literal: He thereupon sent Shide by a side route to break Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent Shide by a secret route to seize Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 完者還救，復敗歸。

translations.literal: Wanzhe returned to relieve it but was again defeated and retreated.
translations.idiomatic: Wanzhe rushed back to relieve the city but was beaten again and driven off.

sentences.zh: 明年，耿炳文取長興，徐達取常州，吳良等取江陰，士誠兵不得四出，勢漸蹙。

translations.literal: The next year Geng Bingwen took Changxing, Xu Da took Changzhou, Wu Liang and others took Jiangyin; Shicheng's troops could not sally in four directions, and his power gradually tightened.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Geng Bingwen took Changxing, Xu Da took Changzhou, and Wu Liang and others took Jiangyin. Shicheng's armies could no longer operate freely, and his position steadily narrowed.

sentences.zh: 亡何，徐達兵徇宜興，攻常熟。

translations.literal: Before long Xu Da's troops overran Yixing and attacked Changshu.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Xu Da overran Yixing and laid siege to Changshu.

sentences.zh: 士德迎戰敗，為前鋒趙德勝所擒。

translations.literal: Shide went out to meet the attack and was defeated; he was captured by the vanguard Zhao Desheng.
translations.idiomatic: Shide marched out to meet them but was defeated and captured by the vanguard Zhao Desheng.

sentences.zh: 士德，小字九六，善戰有謀，能得士心，浙西地皆其所略定。

translations.literal: Shide, childhood name Jiuliu, was skilled in battle and possessed strategy, could win soldiers' hearts, and all the lands of western Zhejiang were what he had seized and settled.
translations.idiomatic: Shide, whose childhood name was Jiuliu, was a skilled and resourceful commander who won the loyalty of his men. It was he who had conquered most of western Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 既被擒，士誠大沮。

translations.literal: Once he was captured, Shicheng was greatly cast down.
translations.idiomatic: When Shide was taken, Shicheng fell into deep despair.

sentences.zh: 太祖欲留士德以招士誠。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor wished to keep Shide to entice Shicheng.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor hoped to keep Shide alive as leverage to win over Shicheng.

sentences.zh: 士德間道貽士誠書，俾降元。

translations.literal: Shide sent a letter to Shicheng by a secret route, ordering him to surrender to the Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Shide smuggled a letter to Shicheng urging him to submit to the Yuan.

sentences.zh: 士誠遂決計請降。

translations.literal: Shicheng thereupon resolved on a plan and requested to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Shicheng thereupon decided to sue for Yuan protection.

sentences.zh: 江浙右丞相達識帖睦邇為言於朝，授士誠太尉，官其將吏有差。

translations.literal: The Jiangzhe Right Chancellor Dashin Temur spoke for him at court; Shicheng was appointed Grand Marshal, and his generals and officials were given offices according to rank.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiangzhe Right Chancellor Dashin Temur pleaded his case at court. Shicheng was appointed Grand Marshal, and his officers received appropriate Yuan posts.

sentences.zh: 士德在金陵竟不食死。

translations.literal: Shide at Jinling in the end starved himself to death.
translations.idiomatic: Shide starved himself to death while held at Jinling.

sentences.zh: 士誠雖去偽號，擅甲兵土地如故。

translations.literal: Although Shicheng set aside his false title, he monopolized arms, troops, and land as before.
translations.idiomatic: Though Shicheng gave up his rebel title, he retained his army and territory as before.

sentences.zh: 達識帖睦邇在杭與楊完者有隙，陰召士誠兵。

translations.literal: Dashin Temur at Hangzhou had a rift with Yang Wanzhe and secretly summoned Shicheng's troops.
translations.idiomatic: Dashin Temur, stationed at Hangzhou, feuded with Yang Wanzhe and secretly called in Shicheng's army.

sentences.zh: 士誠遣史文炳襲殺完者，遂有杭州。

translations.literal: Shicheng sent Shi Wenbing in a surprise attack to kill Wanzhe and thereby obtained Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shicheng sent Shi Wenbing to ambush and kill Wanzhe, and thereby seized Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 順帝遣使征糧，賜之龍衣禦酒。

translations.literal: The Shundi Emperor sent envoys to levy grain and bestowed on him dragon robes and imperial wine.
translations.idiomatic: The Shundi Emperor sent envoys to collect grain tribute and rewarded him with imperial robes and wine.

sentences.zh: 士誠自海道輸糧十一萬石於大都，歲以為常。

translations.literal: Shicheng by the sea route transported one hundred ten thousand piculs of grain to Dadu, and this became annual custom.
translations.idiomatic: Shicheng shipped one hundred ten thousand piculs of grain annually to Dadu by sea, and this became a fixed obligation.

sentences.zh: 既而益驕，令其下頌功德，邀王爵。

translations.literal: Before long he grew ever more arrogant, ordered his subordinates to chant his merits and virtues, and sought a princely title.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he grew still more arrogant, had his followers praise his merit and virtue, and sought a royal enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 不許。

translations.literal: This was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: The request was refused.

sentences.zh: 二十三年九月，士誠復自立為吳王，尊其母曹氏為王太妃，置官屬，別治府第於城中，以士信為浙江行省左丞相，幽達識帖睦邇於嘉興。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the twenty-third year, Shicheng again declared himself King of Wu on his own authority, honored his mother Lady Cao as Queen Dowager, established official appointments, set up a separate government residence in the city, made Shixin Left Chancellor of the Zhejiang Branch Secretariat, and confined Dashin Temur at Jiaxing.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of Zhizheng 23 (1363), Shicheng again proclaimed himself King of Wu, ennobled his mother Lady Cao as Queen Dowager, appointed a full court, established a separate palace within the city, named Shixin Left Chancellor of the Zhejiang Branch Secretariat, and detained Dashin Temur at Jiaxing.

sentences.zh: 元征糧不復與。

translations.literal: The Yuan no longer provided levied grain.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuan court ceased supplying him with levy grain.

sentences.zh: 參軍俞思齊者，字中孚，泰州人，諫士誠曰：「向為賊，可無貢；

translations.literal: Military Adviser Yu Siqi, styled Zhongfu, a man of Taizhou, remonstrated with Shicheng, saying: "Formerly as a bandit one could go without tribute;
translations.idiomatic: Yu Siqi, a military adviser styled Zhongfu and a native of Taizhou, remonstrated with Shicheng: "When you were still a rebel, paying no tribute was understandable;

sentences.zh: 今為臣，不貢可乎？

translations.literal: Now as a subject, can one go without tribute?
translations.idiomatic: but now that you are a subject of the court, can you refuse tribute?

sentences.zh: 」士誠怒，抵案僕地，思齊即引疾去。

translations.literal: Shicheng in anger struck the desk and knocked him down; Siqi immediately pleaded illness and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Shicheng flew into a rage, slammed the desk and knocked him down. Siqi at once resigned on grounds of illness and left.

sentences.zh: 當是時，士誠所據，南抵紹興，北逾徐州，達于濟甯之金溝，西距汝、潁、濠、泗，東薄海，二千餘里，帶甲數十萬。

translations.literal: At that time the territory Shicheng held reached south to Shaoxing, north beyond Xuzhou to Jingou in Jining, west bordered Ru, Ying, Hao, and Si, east pressed upon the sea—more than two thousand li, with several hundred thousand armored troops.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Shicheng's domain stretched more than two thousand li from Shaoxing in the south to beyond Xuzhou and Jingou in Jining in the north, from the Ru, Ying, Hao, and Si region in the west to the sea in the east, and he fielded several hundred thousand armored men.

sentences.zh: 以士信及女夫潘元紹為腹心，左丞徐義、李伯升、呂珍為爪牙，參軍黃敬夫、蔡彥文、葉德新主謀議，元學士陳基、右丞饒介典文章。

translations.literal: He took Shixin and his son-in-law Pan Yuanshao as inner confidants; Left Vice Ministers Xu Yi, Li Bosheng, and Lü Zhen as claws and teeth; Military Advisers Huang Jingfu, Cai Yanwen, and Ye Dexin as masters of counsel; Yuan Academician Chen Ji and Right Vice Minister Rao Jie as masters of literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: Shixin and his son-in-law Pan Yuanshao served as his inner circle; Xu Yi, Li Bosheng, and Lü Zhen were his chief lieutenants; Huang Jingfu, Cai Yanwen, and Ye Dexin handled strategy; and the Yuan academician Chen Ji and Right Vice Minister Rao Jie oversaw state papers and prose.

sentences.zh: 又好招延賓客，所贈遺輿馬、居室、什器甚具。

translations.literal: He also loved to attract and retain guests; what he bestowed in carriages, horses, dwellings, and utensils was very complete.
translations.idiomatic: He also lavishly patronized guests, bestowing carriages, horses, houses, and furnishings in full measure.

sentences.zh: 諸僑寓貧無籍者爭趨之。

translations.literal: Various sojourners who were poor and without registry rushed to join him in competition.
translations.idiomatic: Poor wanderers without local registration flocked to his court.

sentences.zh: 士誠為人，外遲重寡言，似有器量，而實無遠圖。

translations.literal: Shicheng as a man outwardly was slow and weighty and spoke little, seeming to possess capacity, but in fact had no far-reaching design.
translations.idiomatic: Outwardly Shicheng was ponderous and taciturn, seeming a man of breadth, but in truth he lacked any long-term vision.

sentences.zh: 既據有吳中，吳承平久，戶口殷盛，士誠漸奢縱，怠於政事。

translations.literal: Once he had seized and held the Wu region, Wu having been at peace a long time with flourishing population, Shicheng gradually grew luxurious and unrestrained and slackened in government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Once he held the Wu region—a land long at peace and thickly populated—Shicheng grew ever more extravagant and neglectful of governance.

sentences.zh: 士信、元紹尤好聚斂，金玉珍寶及古法書名畫，無不充牣。

translations.literal: Shixin and Yuanshao especially loved to amass wealth; gold, jade, treasures, and famous ancient books and paintings—none failed to fill rooms to overflowing.
translations.idiomatic: Shixin and Yuanshao were especially avid hoarders; gold, jade, jewels, and antique books and paintings packed their halls to overflowing.

sentences.zh: 日夜歌舞自娛。

translations.literal: Day and night they sang and danced to amuse themselves.
translations.idiomatic: They spent day and night in song and dance for their own pleasure.

sentences.zh: 將帥亦偃蹇不用命，每有攻戰，輒稱疾，邀官爵田宅然後起。

translations.literal: The generals also were arrogant and disobedient; whenever there was battle they would claim illness and demand titles, stipends, and estates before they would rise to serve.
translations.idiomatic: His commanders too were insubordinate and high-handed; at every campaign they feigned illness and would fight only after being rewarded with rank, stipends, and estates.

sentences.zh: 甫至軍，所載婢妾樂器踵相接不絕，或大會游談之士，樗蒲蹴踘，皆不以軍務為意。

translations.literal: Barely upon reaching the army, the concubines and musical instruments they brought followed one after another without cease; or they would hold great gatherings of wandering conversationalists, playing dice and cuju—none took military affairs to heart.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching camp they trailed long processions of concubines and musicians, or held lavish parties with idle talkers over dice and cuju, never minding the business of war.

sentences.zh: 及喪師失地還，士誠概置不問。

translations.literal: When they returned after losing armies and territory, Shicheng generally let the matter rest without inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: When they returned after defeats that cost troops and territory, Shicheng asked no questions.

sentences.zh: 已，復用為將。

translations.literal: Before long he again employed them as generals.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he would appoint them to command again.

sentences.zh: 上下嬉娛，以至於亡。

translations.literal: Above and below made merry, until ruin.
translations.idiomatic: The court sank into pleasure from top to bottom until the end came.

sentences.zh: 太祖與士誠接境。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor and Shicheng shared a border.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor and Shicheng now shared a common frontier.

sentences.zh: 士誠數以兵攻常州、江陰、建德、長興、諸全，輒不利去。

translations.literal: Shicheng repeatedly sent troops to attack Changzhou, Jiangyin, Jiande, Changxing, and Zhuquan, but each time without success withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Shicheng repeatedly attacked Changzhou, Jiangyin, Jiande, Changxing, and Zhuquan, but always withdrew without success.

sentences.zh: 而太祖遣邵榮攻湖州，胡大海攻紹興，常遇春攻杭州，亦皆不能下。

translations.literal: Yet the Founding Emperor sent Shao Rong to attack Huzhou, Hu Dahai to attack Shaoxing, and Chang Yuchun to attack Hangzhou—these too all could not be taken.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor's columns under Shao Rong, Hu Dahai, and Chang Yuchun against Huzhou, Shaoxing, and Hangzhou fared no better; none of the cities fell.

sentences.zh: 廖永安被執，謝再興叛降士誠，會太祖與陳友諒相持，未暇及也。

translations.literal: Liao Yong'an was captured; Xie Zaixing rebelled and surrendered to Shicheng; but as the Founding Emperor was locked in stalemate with Chen Youliang, he had no leisure to attend to this.
translations.idiomatic: Liao Yong'an was taken prisoner and Xie Zaixing defected to Shicheng, but the Founding Emperor was then fully engaged against Chen Youliang and could not yet turn his attention there.

sentences.zh: 友諒亦遣使約士誠夾攻太祖，而士誠欲守境觀變，許使者，卒不行。

translations.literal: Youliang also sent envoys to arrange with Shicheng a pincer attack on the Founding Emperor, but Shicheng wished to hold his border and watch how things changed; he assented to the envoys but in the end did not act.
translations.idiomatic: Youliang sent envoys proposing a joint assault on the Founding Emperor, but Shicheng preferred to hold his ground and wait; he gave the envoys a favorable answer yet never moved.

sentences.zh: 太祖既平武昌，師還，即命徐達等規取准東，克泰州、通州，圍高郵。

translations.literal: Once the Founding Emperor had pacified Wuchang, the army returned and he immediately ordered Xu Da and others to plan the seizure of eastern Huai, captured Taizhou and Tongzhou, and besieged Gaoyou.
translations.idiomatic: After pacifying Wuchang the Founding Emperor sent Xu Da and others to secure the Huai region; they took Taizhou and Tongzhou and besieged Gaoyou.

sentences.zh: 士誠以舟師溯江來援，太祖自將擊走之。

translations.literal: Shicheng with a fleet went upriver to relieve them; the Founding Emperor personally led troops and drove him off.
translations.idiomatic: Shicheng sailed upriver with a fleet to relieve the city, but the Founding Emperor personally led his forces and drove him back.

sentences.zh: 達等遂拔高郵，取淮安，悉定淮北地。

translations.literal: Xu Da and the others thereupon took Gaoyou, seized Huai'an, and fully settled the lands north of the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Da and his colleagues then took Gaoyou and Huai'an and secured the entire region north of the Huai.

sentences.zh: 於是移檄平江，數士誠八罪。

translations.literal: Thereupon they issued a proclamation to Pingjiang, enumerating eight crimes of Shicheng.
translations.idiomatic: They then issued a manifesto against Pingjiang listing eight counts against Shicheng.

sentences.zh: 徐達、常遇春帥兵自太湖趨湖州，吳人迎戰於毘山，又戰於七里橋，皆敗，遂圍湖州。

translations.literal: Xu Da and Chang Yuchun led troops from Lake Tai toward Huzhou; Wu forces met them in battle at Pishan and again at Qili Bridge—all were defeated, and Huzhou was thereupon besieged.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Da and Chang Yuchun marched from Lake Tai on Huzhou; Wu armies fought them at Pishan and Qili Bridge, lost both engagements, and the city was besieged.

sentences.zh: 士誠遣硃暹、五太子等以六萬眾來援，屯於舊館，築五砦自固。

translations.literal: Shicheng sent Zhu Xian, the Fifth Prince, and others with sixty thousand men to relieve them; they encamped at Jiuguan and built five stockades to secure themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Shicheng dispatched Zhu Xian, the Fifth Prince, and others with sixty thousand men to the relief; they camped at Jiuguan and threw up five fortified positions.

sentences.zh: 達、遇春築十壘以遮之，斷其糧道。

translations.literal: Xu Da and Chang Yuchun built ten fortifications to block them and cut off their grain route.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Da and Chang Yuchun erected ten blockhouses to intercept them and severed their supply lines.

sentences.zh: 士誠知事急，親督兵來戰，敗于皁林。

translations.literal: Shicheng, knowing affairs were urgent, personally supervised troops to come fight and was defeated at Zaolin.
translations.idiomatic: Realizing the crisis, Shicheng personally led troops into battle and was beaten at Zaolin.

sentences.zh: 其將徐志堅敗於東遷，潘元紹敗于烏鎮，升山水陸寨皆破，舊館援絕，五太子、硃暹、呂珍皆降。

translations.literal: His general Xu Zhijian was defeated at Dongqian, Pan Yuanshao was defeated at Wuzhen, the Shengshan land-and-water camps were all broken, relief at Jiuguan was cut off, and the Fifth Prince, Zhu Xian, and Lü Zhen all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Zhijian was routed at Dongqian, Pan Yuanshao at Wuzhen, the Shengshan river forts were overrun, the Jiuguan relief force was isolated, and the Fifth Prince, Zhu Xian, and Lü Zhen all surrendered.

sentences.zh: 五太子者，士誠養子，短小精悍，能平地躍丈餘，又善沒水，珍、暹皆宿將善戰，至是降。

translations.literal: The Fifth Prince was Shicheng's adopted son—short in stature, keen and fierce, able on level ground to leap more than a zhang, and also skilled at diving underwater; Zhen and Xian were both veteran generals skilled in battle, and at this time surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: The Fifth Prince was Shicheng's adopted son—a compact, ferocious fighter who could leap more than ten feet from a standstill and dive with uncommon skill. Lü Zhen and Zhu Xian were seasoned warriors; now they too submitted.

sentences.zh: 達等以徇於湖州。

translations.literal: Xu Da and the others displayed them as warning at Huzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Da paraded the captives before the walls of Huzhou.

sentences.zh: 守將李伯升等以城降，嘉興、松江相繼降。

translations.literal: The defending generals Li Bosheng and others surrendered the city; Jiaxing and Songjiang in succession surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison commander Li Bosheng surrendered the city, and Jiaxing and Songjiang followed suit.

sentences.zh: 潘原明亦以杭州降于李文忠。

translations.literal: Pan Yuanming also surrendered Hangzhou to Li Wenzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Yuanming likewise surrendered Hangzhou to Li Wenzhong.

sentences.zh: 二十六年十一月，大軍進攻平江，築長圍困之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the twenty-sixth year, the great army advanced to attack Pingjiang, built a long encirclement, and besieged it.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of Zhizheng 26 (1366), the main army advanced on Pingjiang, threw up a cordon, and settled in for a siege.

sentences.zh: 士誠距守數月。

translations.literal: Shicheng resisted and held out for several months.
translations.idiomatic: Shicheng held the city for several months.

sentences.zh: 太祖貽書招之曰：「古之豪傑，以畏天順民為賢，以全身保族為智，漢竇融、宋錢俶是也。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor sent him a letter to win him over, saying: "Ancient heroes regarded revering Heaven and obeying the people as virtue, and preserving oneself and one's clan as wisdom—Han Dou Rong and Song Qian Chu were such men.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor wrote urging surrender: "Great men of old valued reverence for Heaven and obedience to the people's will, and prized the wisdom of saving their own lives and their clans—Dou Rong of Han and Qian Chu of Song were such men.

sentences.zh: 爾宜三思，勿自取夷滅，為天下笑。

translations.literal: You ought to think thrice; do not bring extinction upon yourself and become the world's laughingstock.
translations.idiomatic: Think carefully; do not invite destruction and become a laughingstock to the world.

sentences.zh: 」士誠不報，數突圍決戰，不利。

translations.literal: Shicheng made no reply; several times he broke out to force decisive battle, without success.
translations.idiomatic: Shicheng did not answer. He sallied repeatedly to break the siege and force a decisive battle, but each attempt failed.

sentences.zh: 李伯升知士誠困甚，遣所善客逾城說士誠曰：「初公所恃者，湖州、嘉興、杭州耳，今皆失矣。

translations.literal: Li Bosheng, knowing Shicheng was extremely beset, sent a favored guest over the wall to persuade Shicheng, saying: "At first what you relied upon was only Huzhou, Jiaxing, and Hangzhou; now all are lost.
translations.idiomatic: Li Bosheng, seeing how desperate Shicheng's position had become, sent a trusted adviser over the wall with this counsel: "Your strength once rested on Huzhou, Jiaxing, and Hangzhou—and all three are gone.

sentences.zh: 獨守此城，恐變從中起，公雖欲死，不可得也。

translations.literal: Holding this city alone, I fear upheaval will arise from within; though you wish to die, it will not be obtainable.
translations.idiomatic: Hold this city alone and revolt may erupt within; even if you wish to die, you may not be permitted to.

sentences.zh: 莫若順天命，遣使金陵，稱公所以歸義救民之意，開城門，幅巾待命，當不失萬戶侯。

translations.literal: Better to obey Heaven's mandate, send envoys to Jinling stating your intention in returning to righteousness and saving the people, open the gates, wait in plain cloth—for this you surely will not lose a marquisate of ten thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Better to accept Heaven's mandate: send envoys to Jinling explaining that you submit to spare the people, open the gates, and await orders in plain dress—you should still receive a marquisate.

sentences.zh: 且公之地，譬如博者，得人之物而復失之，于公何損？

translations.literal: Moreover your territory is like a gambler's stake—you gained another's possessions and then lost them again; what loss is there to you?
translations.idiomatic: And your lands are like a gambler's winnings—taken and then lost again; what do you truly forfeit?

sentences.zh: 」士誠仰觀良久曰：「吾將思之。

translations.literal: Shicheng looked upward a long while and said: "I shall think on it.
translations.idiomatic: Shicheng gazed upward for a long moment and said, "I will consider it.

sentences.zh: 」乃謝客，竟不降。

translations.literal: He then dismissed the guest and in the end did not surrender.
translations.idiomatic: He thanked the visitor and sent him away—but in the end he would not submit.

sentences.zh: 士誠故有勇勝軍號「十條龍」者，皆驍猛善鬥，每被銀鎧錦衣出入陣中，至是亦悉敗，溺萬里橋下死。

translations.literal: Shicheng formerly had a Brave Victory Army called the "Ten Dragons"—all fierce and skilled in combat, each time wearing silver armor and brocade robes when entering the battle array; at this time too all were defeated and drowned beneath Wanli Bridge to death.
translations.idiomatic: Shicheng's elite "Ten Dragons" unit—ferocious fighters who rode into battle in silver armor and brocade—was annihilated; they drowned beneath Wanli Bridge.

sentences.zh: 最後丞相士信中礮死，城中洶洶無固志。

translations.literal: Finally the Chancellor Shixin was killed by bombardment; within the city there was uproar and no firm will to hold.
translations.idiomatic: In the end Chancellor Shixin was killed by cannon fire, and panic spread through the city; morale collapsed.

sentences.zh: 二十七年九月，城破，士誠收余眾戰于萬壽寺東街，眾散走。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the twenty-seventh year the city fell; Shicheng gathered the remaining host and fought on East Street of Wanshou Temple; the crowd scattered and fled.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of Zhizheng 27 (1367) the walls were breached. Shicheng rallied his remaining troops for a last stand on East Street by Wanshou Temple, but his men broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 倉皇歸府第，拒戶自縊。

translations.literal: In panic he returned to his residence, barred the door, and hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: He rushed back to his palace, bolted the door, and tried to hang himself.

sentences.zh: 故部將趙世雄解之。

translations.literal: His former subordinate general Zhao Shixiong cut him down and freed him.
translations.idiomatic: His old officer Zhao Shixiong cut him down and saved his life.

sentences.zh: 大將軍達數遣李伯升、潘元紹等諭意，士誠瞑目不答。

translations.literal: Grand General Xu Da repeatedly sent Li Bosheng, Pan Yuanshao, and others to convey his intent; Shicheng closed his eyes and made no answer.
translations.idiomatic: Grand General Xu Da sent Li Bosheng, Pan Yuanshao, and others repeatedly to reason with him, but Shicheng kept his eyes shut and would not speak.

sentences.zh: 舁出葑門，入舟，不復食。

translations.literal: He was carried out through Fumen Gate, put aboard a boat, and no longer ate.
translations.idiomatic: He was borne out through Fumen Gate, placed aboard a boat, and refused all food.

sentences.zh: 至金陵，竟自縊死，年四十七。

translations.literal: Upon reaching Jinling he in the end hanged himself to death, aged forty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: At Jinling he finally hanged himself. He was forty-seven.

sentences.zh: 命具棺葬之。

translations.literal: An order was issued to prepare a coffin and bury him.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor ordered a coffin prepared and had him buried.

sentences.zh: 方士誠之被圍也，語其妻劉曰：「吾敗且死矣，若曹何為？

translations.literal: When Shicheng was besieged he spoke to his wife Lady Liu, saying: "I am defeated and about to die; what will you all do?
