translations.idiomatic: During the siege Shicheng told his wife Lady Liu, "I am beaten and will soon die. What will become of you?

sentences.zh: 」劉答曰：「君無憂，妾必不負君。

translations.literal: Liu answered: "My lord need not worry; your handmaid surely will not fail you.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Liu replied, "Do not fear, my lord—I will not fail you.

sentences.zh: 」積薪齊雲樓下。

translations.literal: She piled firewood beneath Qiyun Tower.
translations.idiomatic: She stacked firewood beneath Qiyun Tower.

sentences.zh: 城破，驅群妾登樓，令養子辰保縱火焚之，亦自縊。

translations.literal: When the city fell she drove the concubines up the tower, ordered the adopted son Chenbao to set fire and burn them, and also hanged herself.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell she sent the concubines up the tower, had her adopted son Chenbao set the firewood ablaze, and hanged herself as well.

sentences.zh: 有二幼子匿民間，不知所終。

translations.literal: Two young sons hid among the common people; their end is unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Two young sons vanished among the people; their fate is unknown.

sentences.zh: 先是，黃敬夫等三人用事，吳人知士誠必敗，有「黃菜葉」十七字之謠，其後卒驗雲。

translations.literal: Earlier Huang Jingfu and the other two held power; the people of Wu knew Shicheng would certainly be defeated; there was a rhyme of seventeen characters, "Yellow Vegetable Leaf," and afterward in the end this was verified as true.
translations.idiomatic: While Huang Jingfu and his two colleagues still ruled, the people of Wu already foresaw Shicheng's downfall in a seventeen-character rhyme playing on the names Huang, Cai, and Ye as "yellow vegetable leaf"—and so it proved.

sentences.zh: 莫天祐者，元末聚眾保無錫州，士誠招之。

translations.literal: Mo Tianyou, at the end of the Yuan gathered a crowd to hold Wuxi Prefecture; Shicheng summoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Mo Tianyou had raised a militia to hold Wuxi in the late Yuan. Shicheng tried to recruit him.

sentences.zh: 不從。

translations.literal: He did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Mo refused.

sentences.zh: 以兵攻之，亦不克。

translations.literal: Shicheng attacked with troops but also could not overcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Shicheng attacked but could not break him.

sentences.zh: 士誠既受元官，天祐乃降。

translations.literal: Once Shicheng had received Yuan offices, Tianyou then surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Only after Shicheng accepted Yuan office did Tianyou submit.

sentences.zh: 士誠累表為同僉樞密院事。

translations.literal: Shicheng repeatedly memorialized on his behalf for Vice Grand Councillor of the Privy Council.
translations.idiomatic: Shicheng repeatedly petitioned the Yuan court to appoint him Vice Councillor of the Privy Council.

sentences.zh: 及平江既圍，他城皆下，惟天祐堅守。

translations.literal: When Pingjiang was already besieged, other cities all fell; only Tianyou firmly held out.
translations.idiomatic: When Pingjiang was under siege and other cities fell one by one, Tianyou alone held firm.

sentences.zh: 士誠破，胡廷瑞急攻之，乃降。

translations.literal: When Shicheng was broken, Hu Tingrui urgently attacked him and he then surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: After Shicheng's defeat Hu Tingrui pressed the attack and Tianyou finally surrendered.

sentences.zh: 太祖以其多傷我兵，誅之。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor because he had greatly harmed our troops executed him.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor had him executed for the heavy losses he had inflicted on Ming forces.

sentences.zh: 李伯升仕士誠至司徒，既降，命仍故官，進中書平章同知詹事府事。

translations.literal: Li Bosheng served Shicheng up to Grand Mentor; once he surrendered he was ordered to retain his former office and was promoted to Vice Grand Councillor of the Secretariat and Associate Administrator of the Heir Apparent's Household.
translations.idiomatic: Li Bosheng had risen to Grand Mentor under Shicheng. After his surrender he kept his rank and was promoted to Vice Grand Councillor of the Secretariat and deputy director of the Heir Apparent's household.

sentences.zh: 嘗將兵討平湖廣慈利蠻，又為征南右副將軍，同吳良討靖州蠻。

translations.literal: He once led troops to subdue the Pinghu Guangcili barbarians; he also served as Right Vice General of the Southern Expedition and together with Wu Liang subdued the Jingzhou barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: He campaigned against the Pinghu and Guangcili tribes and later served as deputy southern expedition commander alongside Wu Liang against the Jingzhou tribes.

sentences.zh: 後坐胡黨死。

translations.literal: Later he was implicated in the Hu faction and died.
translations.idiomatic: He was later executed as an associate of Hu Weiyong's faction.

sentences.zh: 潘元明以平章守杭州降，仍為行省平章，與伯升俱歲食祿七百五十石，不治事。

translations.literal: Pan Yuanming as Branch Secretariat Administrator guarding Hangzhou surrendered; he remained Branch Secretariat Administrator, and together with Bosheng each received seven hundred fifty shi of grain annually, without administering affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Yuanming surrendered Hangzhou while serving as Branch Secretariat Administrator; he kept that title and, like Bosheng, received an annual stipend of seven hundred fifty shi without active duties.

sentences.zh: 雲南平，以元明署布政司事，卒官。

translations.literal: When Yunnan was pacified he was appointed to administer Provincial Administration Commission affairs and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: After Yunnan was pacified he was put in charge of the provincial administration commission and died in office.

sentences.zh: 士誠自起至亡，凡十四年。

translations.literal: From Shicheng's rise to his destruction, altogether fourteen years.
translations.idiomatic: From his first rising to his final fall, Shicheng's cause lasted fourteen years.

sentences.zh: 方國珍

translations.literal: Fang Guozhen
translations.idiomatic: Fang Guozhen

sentences.zh: 方國珍，黃岩人。

translations.literal: Fang Guozhen was a man of Huangyan.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Guozhen was a native of Huangyan.

sentences.zh: 長身黑面，體白如瓠，力逐奔馬。

translations.literal: He was tall of body and black of face, his torso pale as a gourd, and his strength could chase down a galloping horse.
translations.idiomatic: He was tall and dark-faced, with a torso pale as a gourd, and strength enough to run down a galloping horse.

sentences.zh: 世以販鹽浮海為業。

translations.literal: For generations his occupation was selling salt and traveling the sea.
translations.idiomatic: His family made their living as salt smugglers plying the coastal trade.

sentences.zh: 元至正八年，有蔡亂頭者，行剽海上，有司發兵捕之。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Yuan Zhizheng there was one Cai Luantou who plundered along the sea; the authorities dispatched troops to capture him.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhizheng 8 (1348) a pirate named Cai Luantou preyed on coastal shipping, and the authorities sent troops against him.

sentences.zh: 國珍怨家告其通寇。

translations.literal: Guozhen's enemy by grievance reported that he had communicated with the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: A personal enemy denounced Guozhen for colluding with the pirates.

sentences.zh: 國珍殺怨家，遂與兄國璋、弟國瑛、國瑉亡入海，聚眾數千人，劫運艘，梗海道。

translations.literal: Guozhen killed the enemy by grievance, then together with elder brother Guozhang and younger brothers Guoying and Guomin fled to the sea, gathered a crowd of several thousand, plundered transport vessels, and obstructed the sea routes.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhen killed his accuser, fled to sea with his brothers Guozhang, Guoying, and Guomin, raised several thousand men, seized grain transports, and choked the shipping lanes.

sentences.zh: 行省參政朵兒只班討之，兵敗，為所執，脅使請於朝，授定海尉。

translations.literal: Branch Secretariat Administrator Dorjiban campaigned against him, the army was defeated, and he was captured by them; they coerced him to petition the court, and Guozhen was appointed Defender of Dinghai.
translations.idiomatic: The Branch Secretariat Administrator Dorjiban marched against him but was defeated and captured. Guozhen forced him to intercede at court and received appointment as Defender of Dinghai.

sentences.zh: 尋叛，寇溫州。

translations.literal: Before long he rebelled and raided Wenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He soon rebelled again and raided Wenzhou.

sentences.zh: 元以孛羅帖木兒為行省左丞，督兵往討，復敗，被執。

translations.literal: The Yuan made Boluo Temur Branch Secretariat Left Vice Minister, supervised troops to campaign against him, was again defeated, and was captured.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuan sent Boluo Temur as Left Vice Minister of the Branch Secretariat to suppress him; he too was beaten and taken prisoner.

sentences.zh: 乃遣大司農達識帖睦邇招之降。

translations.literal: Thereupon they dispatched the Grand Secretary of Agriculture Dashin Temur to summon him to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: The court then sent Dashin Temur, Grand Secretary of Agriculture, to negotiate his surrender.

sentences.zh: 已而汝、潁兵起，元募舟師守江。

translations.literal: Before long troops rose in Ru and Ying; the Yuan recruited a fleet to guard the river.
translations.idiomatic: When rebellion erupted in the Ru and Ying region the Yuan recruited a river fleet for defense.

sentences.zh: 國珍疑懼，復叛。

translations.literal: Guozhen was suspicious and afraid and rebelled again.
translations.idiomatic: Fearful and uncertain, Guozhen rebelled once more.

sentences.zh: 誘殺台州路達魯花赤泰不華，亡入海。

translations.literal: He lured and killed Taibuhua, Darughachi of Taizhou Circuit, and fled to the sea.
translations.idiomatic: He tricked and killed Taibuhua, the Mongol governor of Taizhou, and fled back to sea.

sentences.zh: 使人潛至京師，賂諸權貴，仍許降，授徽州路治中。

translations.literal: He sent men secretly to the capital, bribed various powerful officials, and was again permitted to surrender and appointed Vice Administrator of Huizhou Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He sent agents to the capital to bribe influential officials, secured another amnesty, and was appointed Vice Administrator of Huizhou.

sentences.zh: 國珍不聽命，陷台州，焚蘇之太倉。

translations.literal: Guozhen did not obey orders, seized Taizhou, and burned Taicang in Su prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhen ignored his orders, seized Taizhou, and burned Taicang in Suzhou prefecture.

sentences.zh: 元復以海道漕運萬戶招之，乃受官。

translations.literal: The Yuan again recruited him with the post of Sea Route Grain Transport Commissioner, and he then accepted office.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuan court lured him back with the post of Sea Route Grain Transport Commissioner, and this time he accepted.

sentences.zh: 尋進行省參政，俾以兵攻張士誠。

translations.literal: Before long he was promoted Branch Secretariat Administrator and ordered with troops to attack Zhang Shicheng.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to Branch Secretariat Administrator and ordered to march against Zhang Shicheng.

sentences.zh: 士誠遣將禦之昆山。

translations.literal: Shicheng sent a general to defend against him at Kunshan.
translations.idiomatic: Shicheng sent a general to meet him at Kunshan.

sentences.zh: 國珍七戰七捷。

translations.literal: Guozhen seven battles seven victories.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhen won seven consecutive victories.

sentences.zh: 會士誠亦降，乃罷兵。

translations.literal: As it happened Shicheng also surrendered, and thereupon he ceased military action.
translations.idiomatic: When Shicheng in turn submitted to the Yuan, Guozhen stood down.

sentences.zh: 先是，天下承平，國珍兄弟始倡亂海上，有司憚於用兵，一意招撫。

translations.literal: Earlier when all under Heaven was at peace, the Guozhen brothers first raised turmoil on the sea; the authorities feared employing troops and devoted themselves solely to appeasement and recruitment.
translations.idiomatic: From the first, while the empire still seemed at peace, the Fang brothers had pioneered piracy on the coast; local officials shrank from military action and relied exclusively on conciliation.

sentences.zh: 惟都事劉基以國珍首逆，數降數叛，不可赦。

translations.literal: Only Commissioner Liu Ji argued that Guozhen was the first rebel, repeatedly surrendering and repeatedly rebelling, and could not be pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Only Commissioner Liu Ji maintained that Guozhen, as the original rebel who had surrendered and rebelled again and again, deserved no pardon.

sentences.zh: 朝議不聽。

translations.literal: The court deliberation did not accept this.
translations.idiomatic: The court would not heed him.

sentences.zh: 國珍既授官，據有慶元、溫、台之地，益強不可制。

translations.literal: Once Guozhen received his appointment, he held Qingyuan, Wen, and Tai, growing ever stronger and beyond control.
translations.idiomatic: Once Guozhen had received his appointment, he held Qingyuan, Wenzhou, and Taizhou and grew so powerful that no one could restrain him.

sentences.zh: 國珍之初作亂也，元出空名宣敕數十道募人擊賊。

translations.literal: When Guozhen first rebelled, the Yuan issued dozens of hollow-title imperial rescripts to recruit men to attack the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: When Guozhen first rose in rebellion, the Yuan court issued dozens of rescripts bearing empty titles, calling on men to join the fight against the rebels.

sentences.zh: 海濱壯士多應募立功。

translations.literal: Many stalwart men of the coast answered the call and achieved merit.
translations.idiomatic: Many bold men of the coast answered the summons and won distinction in battle.

sentences.zh: 所司邀重賄，不輒與，有一家數人死事卒不得官者。

translations.literal: The responsible offices demanded heavy bribes and did not readily grant appointments; there were families in which several men died in service yet never received office.
translations.idiomatic: The offices in charge demanded heavy bribes and would not readily grant commissions; some families lost several men in the fighting and still never received an appointment.

sentences.zh: 而國珍之徒，一再招諭，皆至大官。

translations.literal: Yet Guozhen's followers, after repeated summons and persuasion, all rose to high office.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Guozhen's men, summoned and placated again and again, all rose to high rank.

sentences.zh: 由是民慕為盜，從國珍者益眾。

translations.literal: Hence the people envied becoming bandits, and those following Guozhen grew ever more numerous.
translations.idiomatic: From this the people came to admire the life of a bandit, and Guozhen's following swelled.

sentences.zh: 元既失江、淮，資國珍舟以通海運，重以官爵羈縻之，而無以難也。

translations.literal: Once the Yuan had lost the Yangtze and Huai regions, they relied on Guozhen's ships for maritime grain transport, rewarding him heavily with offices and titles to keep him bound, yet had no means to restrain him.
translations.idiomatic: After the Yuan lost the Yangtze and Huai regions, they depended on Guozhen's fleet for the sea route of the grain tribute and tried to tether him with lavish offices and titles, yet had no real leverage over him.

sentences.zh: 有張子善者，好縱橫術，說國珍以師溯江窺江東，北略青、徐、遼海。

translations.literal: There was one Zhang Zishan, who loved the arts of alliance and stratagem; he urged Guozhen to lead his army up the Yangtze to probe Jiangdong, and northward to seize Qing, Xu, and the Liaohai region.
translations.idiomatic: One Zhang Zishan, a devotee of alliance and stratagem, urged Guozhen to march his forces up the Yangtze and probe Jiangdong, then strike north toward Qingzhou, Xuzhou, and the Liaohai coast.

sentences.zh: 國珍曰：「吾始志不及此。

translations.literal: Guozhen said: "My initial ambition did not extend this far."
translations.idiomatic: Guozhen said, "My ambitions never reached that far."

sentences.zh: 」謝之去。

translations.literal: He declined and sent him away.
translations.idiomatic: He thanked him and sent him on his way.

sentences.zh: 太祖已取婺州，使主簿蔡元剛使慶元。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor had already taken Wuzhou and sent Registrar Cai Yuangang as envoy to Qingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor had already seized Wuzhou and dispatched Registrar Cai Yuangang as envoy to Qingyuan.

sentences.zh: 國珍謀於其下曰：「江左號令嚴明，恐不能與抗。

translations.literal: Guozhen consulted his subordinates, saying: "Left of the Yangtze, their orders are strict and clear; I fear we cannot resist them."
translations.idiomatic: Guozhen consulted his subordinates and said, "The regime south of the Yangtze keeps strict discipline; I fear we cannot stand against it."

sentences.zh: 況為我敵者，西有吳，南有閩。

translations.literal: Moreover, those who are our enemies — to the west is Wu, to the south is Min.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, we already have enemies to the west in Wu and to the south in Min."

sentences.zh: 莫若姑示順從，藉為聲援以觀變。

translations.literal: Better for now to show compliance, borrowing them as a supporting voice while watching how events unfold.
translations.idiomatic: Better to feign obedience for the moment, use them as a backing voice, and wait to see how affairs turn."

sentences.zh: 」眾以為然。

translations.literal: The group agreed.
translations.idiomatic: The assembly agreed.

sentences.zh: 於是遣使奉書進黃金五十斤，白金百斤，文綺百匹。

translations.literal: Thereupon he sent envoys bearing a letter and presenting fifty jin of gold, one hundred jin of silver, and one hundred bolts of patterned silk.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent envoys with a letter and gifts of fifty jin of gold, one hundred jin of silver, and one hundred bolts of brocade.

sentences.zh: 太祖復遣鎮撫孫養浩報之。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor in turn sent Pacification Commissioner Sun Yanghao to reply.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor sent Pacification Commissioner Sun Yanghao in reply.

sentences.zh: 國珍請以溫、台、慶元三郡獻，且遣次子關為質。

translations.literal: Guozhen requested to offer the three prefectures of Wen, Tai, and Qingyuan, and furthermore sent his second son Guan as hostage.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhen offered to surrender the three prefectures of Wenzhou, Taizhou, and Qingyuan and sent his second son Guan as a hostage.

sentences.zh: 太祖卻其質，厚賜而遣之；

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor refused the hostage, richly rewarded him, and sent him back;
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor declined the hostage, gave him rich gifts, and sent him home;

sentences.zh: 復使博士夏煜往，拜國珍福建行省平章事，弟國瑛參知政事，國瑉樞密分院僉事。

translations.literal: again sent Scholar Xia Yu to appoint Guozhen Minister of the Branch Secretariat of Fujian Province, his younger brother Guoying as Vice Minister, and Guomin as an official of the Secretariat Branch.
translations.idiomatic: he then sent Academician Xia Yu to invest Guozhen as Minister of the Fujian Branch Secretariat, his brother Guoying as Vice Minister, and Guomin as an official of the Secretariat Branch.

sentences.zh: 國珍名獻三郡，實陰持兩端。

translations.literal: Guozhen nominally offered the three prefectures, but in fact secretly maintained a foot in both camps.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhen made a show of surrendering the three prefectures but secretly kept one foot in each camp.

sentences.zh: 煜既至，乃詐稱疾，自言老不任職，惟受平章印誥而已。

translations.literal: When Yu arrived, Guozhen falsely claimed illness, saying he was too old to hold office and accepted only the minister's seal and patent.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu arrived, Guozhen feigned illness, saying he was too old to serve and would accept only the minister's seal and commission.

sentences.zh: 太祖察其情，以書諭曰：「吾始以汝豪傑識時務，故命汝專制一方。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor perceived his motives and wrote to instruct him: "At first I took you for a hero who understood the times, and therefore appointed you to sole rule of one region."
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor saw through him and wrote: "At first I took you for a man of talent who knew the times, and therefore entrusted you with sole rule of one region."

sentences.zh: 汝顧中懷叵測，欲覘我虛實則遣侍子，欲卻我官爵則稱老病。

translations.literal: Yet you harbor inscrutable designs within: to probe my strength and weakness you send your son in attendance; to reject my offices and titles you claim old age and illness.
translations.idiomatic: Yet your heart is unreadable: you send your son to court to spy on my strength, and plead old age and sickness to refuse my offices and titles.

sentences.zh: 夫智者轉敗為功，賢者因禍成福，汝審圖之。

translations.literal: The wise turn defeat into achievement; the worthy turn misfortune into blessing — consider this carefully.
translations.idiomatic: The wise turn defeat into victory; the worthy turn disaster into blessing. Weigh this well.

sentences.zh: 」是時國珍歲歲治海舟，為元氵曹張士誠粟十余萬石于京師，元累進國珍官至江浙行省左丞相衢國公，分省慶元。

translations.literal: At this time Guozhen every year maintained seagoing vessels, transporting over one hundred thousand shi of Zhang Shicheng's grain to the capital for the Yuan grain transport; the Yuan repeatedly promoted Guozhen to Left Chancellor of the Branch Secretariat of Zhejiang and Jiangsu, Duke of Qu, with his branch secretariat at Qingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Guozhen kept a fleet in repair year after year, shipping more than one hundred thousand shi of Zhang Shicheng's grain to the capital for the Yuan grain transport. The Yuan repeatedly promoted him to Left Chancellor of the Zhejiang-Jiangsu Branch Secretariat and Duke of Qu, with his secretariat seated at Qingyuan.

sentences.zh: 國珍受之如故，特以甘言謝太祖，絕無內附意。

translations.literal: Guozhen accepted these as before, merely offering honeyed words of thanks to the Founding Emperor, with absolutely no intention of inward submission.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhen accepted these honors as before, offering only honeyed thanks to the Founding Emperor and showing not the slightest intent to submit in earnest.

sentences.zh: 及得所諭書，竟不省。

translations.literal: When he received the letter of instruction, he paid it no heed at all.
translations.idiomatic: When he received the Founding Emperor's letter of admonition, he ignored it entirely.

sentences.zh: 太祖復以書諭曰：「福基於至誠，禍生於反覆，隗囂、公孫述故轍可鑒。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor again wrote to instruct him: "Blessing rests on utmost sincerity; calamity rises from vacillation — the old tracks of Wei Xiao and Gongsun Shu may serve as a mirror."
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor wrote again: "Fortune rests on utmost sincerity; disaster springs from vacillation. The fates of Wei Xiao and Gongsun Shu stand as a warning."

sentences.zh: 大軍一出，不可虛辭解也。

translations.literal: Once the great army marches forth, empty words will not avail.
translations.idiomatic: Once the great army moves, fine words will no longer suffice."

sentences.zh: 」國珍詐窮，復陽為惶懼謝罪，以金寶飾鞍馬獻。

translations.literal: Guozhen, his deceptions exhausted, again feigned fear and alarm to beg forgiveness, presenting saddle-horses adorned with gold and jewels.
translations.idiomatic: His stratagems exhausted, Guozhen again put on a show of fear and remorse and sent saddle-horses adorned with gold and jewels.

sentences.zh: 太祖復卻之。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor again refused them.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor refused them once more.

sentences.zh: 已而苗帥蔣英等叛，殺胡大海，持首奔國珍，國珍不受，自台州奔福建。

translations.literal: Before long the Miao commander Jiang Ying and others rebelled, killed Hu Dahai, and fled with his head to Guozhen; Guozhen did not accept them, and they fled from Taizhou to Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Miao commander Jiang Ying and others mutinied, killed Hu Dahai, and fled with his head to Guozhen. Guozhen would not receive them, and they escaped from Taizhou into Fujian.

sentences.zh: 國璋守台，邀擊之，為所敗，被殺，太祖遣使弔祭。

translations.literal: Guozhang defended Taizhou, intercepted and attacked them, was defeated and killed; the Founding Emperor sent envoys to mourn and sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhang, holding Taizhou, intercepted them but was defeated and killed. The Founding Emperor sent envoys to mourn and offer sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 逾年，溫人周宗道以平陽來降。

translations.literal: A year later, Zhou Zongdao of Wenzhou came to surrender with Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Zhou Zongdao of Wenzhou surrendered with Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 國珍從子明善守溫以兵爭。

translations.literal: Guozhen's nephew Mingshan held Wenzhou and fought with troops to contest it.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhen's nephew Mingshan held Wenzhou and fought to keep it.

sentences.zh: 參軍胡深擊敗之，遂下里安，進兵溫州。

translations.literal: Staff Officer Hu Shen defeated him, then took Li'an and advanced on Wenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Staff Officer Hu Shen routed him, took Li'an, and marched on Wenzhou.

sentences.zh: 國珍恐，請歲輸白金三萬兩給軍，俟杭州下，即納土來歸。

translations.literal: Guozhen grew fearful and requested to pay thirty thousand taels of silver annually to supply the army, pledging that once Hangzhou fell he would surrender his territory and submit.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Guozhen offered to pay thirty thousand taels of silver each year to supply the army and promised that once Hangzhou fell he would surrender his lands and submit.

sentences.zh: 太祖詔深班師。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor ordered Shen to withdraw the army.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor ordered Hu Shen to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 九月，太祖已破平江，命參政硃亮祖攻台州，國瑛迎戰敗走。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, the Founding Emperor having already taken Pingjiang, ordered Vice Minister Zhu Liangzu to attack Taizhou; Guoying met him in battle and fled in defeat.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, with Pingjiang already fallen, the Founding Emperor ordered Vice Minister Zhu Liangzu against Taizhou. Guoying met him in battle and fled in defeat.

sentences.zh: 進克溫州。

translations.literal: He advanced and captured Wenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed on and captured Wenzhou.

sentences.zh: 征南將軍湯和以大軍長驅抵慶元。

translations.literal: The Southern Campaign General Tang He with a great army drove in a long march to Qingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Southern Campaign General Tang He marched at the head of a great army straight to Qingyuan.

sentences.zh: 國珍帥所部遁入海。

translations.literal: Guozhen led his followers and fled onto the sea.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhen led his followers and fled out to sea.

sentences.zh: 追敗之盤嶼，其部將相次降。

translations.literal: Pursuing, they defeated him at Pan Island; his subordinate generals surrendered one after another.
translations.idiomatic: The pursuers routed him at Pan Island, and his commanders surrendered one after another.

sentences.zh: 和數令人示以順逆，國珍乃遣子關奉表乞降曰：「臣聞天無所不覆，地無所不載。

translations.literal: He repeatedly sent men to show the consequences of submission and rebellion; Guozhen thereupon sent his son Guan with a memorial begging to surrender, saying: "Your subject has heard that Heaven covers all and Earth bears all."
translations.idiomatic: Tang He repeatedly sent men to spell out the price of obedience and rebellion. Guozhen then sent his son Guan with a memorial begging to surrender: "Your subject has heard that Heaven covers all and Earth bears all."

sentences.zh: 王者體天法地，於人無所不容。

translations.literal: A king embodies Heaven and follows Earth's law, excluding no one.
translations.idiomatic: A true king takes Heaven as his model and Earth as his law, and excludes no man."

sentences.zh: 臣荷主上覆載之德舊矣，不敢自絕於天地，故一陳愚衷。

translations.literal: Your subject has long received the emperor's covering and bearing grace, and dares not cut himself off from Heaven and Earth; therefore I lay bare my foolish heart once.
translations.idiomatic: Long have I owed Your Majesty the grace of Heaven's cover and Earth's bearing, and I dare not cut myself off from them; therefore I lay my foolish heart bare once."

sentences.zh: 臣本庸才，遭時多故，起身海島，非有父兄相藉之力，又非有帝制自為之心。

translations.literal: Your subject is by nature a mediocre talent; encountering turbulent times, I rose from a sea isle — without the support of father and elder brothers, and without any heart to claim imperial rule for myself.
translations.idiomatic: I am a man of no great talent. Caught in troubled times, I rose from a sea isle without the backing of father or elder brothers, and never with any heart to claim the throne for myself."

sentences.zh: 方主上霆擊電掣，至於婺州，臣愚即遣子入侍，固已知主上有今日矣，將以依日月之末光，望雨露之餘潤。

translations.literal: When Your Majesty struck like thunder and lightning, reaching Wuzhou, this fool at once sent his son into attendance, already knowing Your Majesty would have this day; I meant to bask in the trailing light of sun and moon, and hope for the lingering moisture of rain and dew.
translations.idiomatic: When Your Majesty struck like thunder and lightning as far as Wuzhou, this fool at once sent his son to court, already knowing Your Majesty would reach this day. I meant only to shelter in the last rays of sun and moon and hope for the lingering dew of rain."

sentences.zh: 而主上推誠布公，俾守鄉郡，如故吳越事。

translations.literal: Yet Your Majesty extended sincerity and fairness, allowing me to guard my native prefectures, as in the old Wu-Yue arrangement.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty then dealt with me in open sincerity and let me keep my home prefectures, as in the old Wu-Yue arrangement."

sentences.zh: 臣遵奉條約，不敢妄生節目。

translations.literal: Your subject obeyed the terms and dared not arbitrarily create complications.
translations.idiomatic: I obeyed every term of our agreement and dared not stir up trouble on my own."

sentences.zh: 子姓不戒，潛構釁端，猥勞問罪之師，私心戰兢，用是俾守者出迎。

translations.literal: My sons and clansmen, lacking caution, secretly provoked trouble; I have presumptuously troubled the punitive army, and in private I tremble with fear — for this reason I had the defenders go out to welcome them.
translations.idiomatic: My sons and clansmen, failing in caution, secretly provoked conflict and presumptuously brought down Your Majesty's punitive force. In my heart I tremble, and for that reason I ordered the garrison to go out and welcome your army."

sentences.zh: 然而未免浮海，何也？

translations.literal: Yet I could not avoid taking to the sea — why?
translations.idiomatic: Yet I still took to the sea — why?"

sentences.zh: 孝子之於親，小杖則受，大杖則走，臣之情事適與此類。

translations.literal: A filial son toward his parent accepts the small rod but flees the great rod; your subject's circumstances fit this pattern exactly.
translations.idiomatic: A filial son accepts the small rod from his parent but flees the great one; my case is exactly of that kind."

sentences.zh: 即欲面縛待罪闕廷，復恐嬰斧鉞之誅，使天下後世不知臣得罪之深，將謂主上不能容臣，豈不累天地大德哉。

translations.literal: Though I wished to bind myself and await judgment at the court, I feared again to invite execution by blade and axe, lest later ages not know how deeply your subject had offended, and say that Your Majesty could not tolerate me — would this not burden Heaven and Earth's great virtue?
translations.idiomatic: Though I wished to bind myself and await judgment at court, I feared again to invite the axe, lest later ages not know how deeply I had offended and conclude that Your Majesty could not forgive me — would that not tarnish Heaven and Earth's great virtue?

sentences.zh: 」蓋幕下士詹鼎詞也。

translations.literal: This was the composition of his staff member Zhan Ding.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was the work of his staff member Zhan Ding.

sentences.zh: 太祖覽而憐之，賜書曰：「汝違吾諭，不即斂手歸命，次且海外，負恩實多。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor read it and took pity, sending a letter: "You disobeyed my instructions, did not at once lay down your arms and submit, but lingered overseas — your ingratitude is indeed great."
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor read it and took pity on him, writing in reply: "You defied my admonitions, did not at once lay down your arms and submit, but lingered overseas — your ingratitude is great indeed."

sentences.zh: 今者窮蹙無聊，情詞哀懇，吾當以汝此誠為誠，不以前過為過，汝勿自疑。

translations.literal: Now, pressed to extremity with nowhere to turn, your words are piteous and earnest; I shall take this sincerity of yours as sincerity, and not hold your former faults against you — do not doubt yourself.
translations.idiomatic: Now, driven to extremity with nowhere to turn, your words are piteous and earnest. I shall take this present sincerity as sincerity and not count your former faults against you. Do not doubt yourself."

sentences.zh: 」遂促國珍入朝，面讓之曰：「若來得毋晚乎！

translations.literal: He then urged Guozhen to come to court, and rebuked him to his face: "Your coming — was it not rather late!"
translations.idiomatic: He then pressed Guozhen to come to court and rebuked him to his face: "Your coming — was it not rather late!"

sentences.zh: 」國珍頓首謝。

translations.literal: Guozhen prostrated himself and apologized.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhen kowtowed and begged forgiveness.

sentences.zh: 授廣西行省左丞，食祿不之官。

translations.literal: He was appointed Left Vice Minister of the Branch Secretariat of Guangxi, drawing salary but not taking up the post.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Left Vice Minister of the Guangxi Branch Secretariat, drawing salary but not taking up the post.

sentences.zh: 數歲，卒于京師。

translations.literal: Several years later, he died in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later he died in the capital.

sentences.zh: 子禮，官廣洋衛指揮僉事；

translations.literal: His son Li held the post of Assistant Commander of the Guangyang Guard;
translations.idiomatic: His son Li served as Assistant Commander of the Guangyang Guard;

sentences.zh: 關，虎賁衛千戶所鎮撫。

translations.literal: Guan served as Pacification Commissioner of a Thousand-Household Unit of the Huben Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Guan served as Pacification Commissioner of a Huben Guard thousand-household unit.

sentences.zh: 關弟行，字明敏，善詩，承旨宋濂嘗稱之。

translations.literal: Guan's younger brother Xing, styled Mingmin, was skilled at poetry; Academician Song Lian once praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Guan's younger brother Xing, styled Mingmin, was a gifted poet whom Academician Song Lian once praised.

sentences.zh: 劉仁本，字德元，國珍同縣人。

translations.literal: Liu Renben, styled Deyuan, was a man of the same county as Guozhen.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Renben, styled Deyuan, was a native of Guozhen's county.

sentences.zh: 元末進士乙科，曆官浙江行省郎中，與張本仁俱入國珍幕。

translations.literal: At the end of the Yuan he passed the second tier of the civil service examination, served successively as Director of the Branch Secretariat of Zhejiang Province, and together with Zhang Benren entered Guozhen's staff.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Yuan he passed the second tier of the civil examinations, rose to Director of the Zhejiang Branch Secretariat, and entered Guozhen's staff together with Zhang Benren.

sentences.zh: 數從名士趙俶、謝理、硃右等賦詩，有稱于時。

translations.literal: He often joined the celebrated literati Zhao Chu, Xie Li, Zhu You, and others in composing poetry, winning renown in his time.
translations.idiomatic: He often composed poetry with the celebrated literati Zhao Chu, Xie Li, Zhu You, and others, and won renown in his day.

sentences.zh: 國珍海運輸元，實仁本司其事。

translations.literal: Guozhen's maritime grain transport to the Yuan was in fact managed by Renben.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhen's maritime grain shipments to the Yuan were in fact directed by Renben.

sentences.zh: 硃亮祖之下溫州也，獲仁本。

translations.literal: When Zhu Liangzu took Wenzhou, Renben was captured.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Liangzu took Wenzhou, Renben was captured.

sentences.zh: 太祖數其罪，鞭背潰爛死。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor enumerated his crimes; he was flogged until his back split open and putrefied, and he died.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor recited his crimes and had him flogged until his back split open and festered; he died of the beating.

sentences.zh: 余官屬從國珍降者皆徙滁州，獨赦丘楠，以為韶州知府。

translations.literal: The remaining officials and followers who surrendered with Guozhen were all relocated to Chuzhou; only Qiu Nan was pardoned and made Prefect of Shaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: The remaining officials and followers who surrendered with Guozhen were all resettled in Chuzhou; only Qiu Nan was pardoned and appointed Prefect of Shaozhou.

sentences.zh: 詹鼎者，寧海人，有才學。

translations.literal: Zhan Ding was a man of Ninghai, talented and learned.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan Ding was a native of Ninghai, a man of talent and learning.

sentences.zh: 為國珍府都事，判上虞，有治聲。

translations.literal: He served as Commissioner of Guozhen's headquarters, administered Shangyu, and had a reputation for good governance.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Commissioner in Guozhen's headquarters, governed Shangyu, and won a reputation for effective rule.

sentences.zh: 既至京，未見用，草封事萬言，候駕出獻之。

translations.literal: Once he reached the capital he was not employed; he drafted a ten-thousand-word sealed memorial and waited for the emperor's departure to present it.
translations.idiomatic: After reaching the capital he went unused; he drafted a ten-thousand-word sealed memorial and waited for the emperor's procession to present it.

sentences.zh: 帝為立馬受讀，命丞相官鼎。

translations.literal: The emperor dismounted from his horse to receive and read it, and ordered the Chancellor to appoint Ding to office.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor dismounted to receive and read it, then ordered the Chancellor to appoint Ding to office.

sentences.zh: 楊憲忌其才，沮之。

translations.literal: Yang Xian envied his talent and obstructed him.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xian, jealous of his talent, blocked the appointment.

sentences.zh: 憲敗，除留守經歷，遷刑部郎中，坐累死。

translations.literal: When Yang fell, Ding was appointed Administrative Aide to the Capital Guard, then promoted to Director of the Ministry of Punishments; he died from overwork in office.
translations.idiomatic: After Yang's fall he was appointed administrative aide to the capital guard, then promoted to Director of the Ministry of Punishments; he died from overwork in office.

sentences.zh: 明玉珍

translations.literal: Ming Yuzhen
translations.idiomatic: Ming Yuzhen

sentences.zh: 明玉珍，隨州人。

translations.literal: Ming Yuzhen was a man of Suizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ming Yuzhen was a native of Suizhou.

sentences.zh: 身長八尺餘，目重瞳子。

translations.literal: He stood over eight chi in height, and his eyes had double pupils.
translations.idiomatic: He stood more than eight chi tall, and his eyes had double pupils.

sentences.zh: 徐壽輝起，玉珍與里中父老團結千餘人，屯青山。

translations.literal: When Xu Shouhui rose, Yuzhen together with the elders of his village gathered more than a thousand men and encamped at Qingshan.
translations.idiomatic: When Xu Shouhui rose in rebellion, Yuzhen joined the village elders in gathering more than a thousand men and encamped at Qingshan.

sentences.zh: 及壽輝稱帝，使人招玉珍曰：「來則共富貴，不來舉兵屠之。

translations.literal: When Shouhui declared himself emperor, he sent men to summon Yuzhen, saying: "Come and we shall share wealth and honor; if you do not come, I shall raise troops and slaughter you."
translations.idiomatic: When Shouhui declared himself emperor, he sent men to summon Yuzhen with the message: "Come and we shall share wealth and rank; if you refuse, I shall raise troops and slaughter you."

sentences.zh: 」玉珍引眾降，以元帥守沔陽。

translations.literal: Yuzhen led his followers to submit and was made Marshal guarding Mianyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yuzhen led his followers in submission and was made Marshal guarding Mianyang.

sentences.zh: 與元將哈麻禿戰湖中，飛矢中右目，遂眇。

translations.literal: Fighting on the lake with the Yuan general Qimaya, a flying arrow struck his right eye, and he was blinded in it.
translations.idiomatic: In a battle on the lake with the Yuan general Qimaya, a stray arrow struck his right eye and blinded him in it.

sentences.zh: 久之，玉珍帥鬥船五十艘掠糧川、峽間，將引還。

translations.literal: After some time, Yuzhen led fifty fighting ships to plunder between Liangchuan and the gorges, and was about to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Some time later Yuzhen led fifty fighting ships to raid between Liangchuan and the gorges and was about to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 時元右丞完者都募兵重慶，義兵元帥楊漢應募至，欲殺之而並其軍，不克。

translations.literal: At that time the Yuan Right Chancellor Wanerdu was recruiting troops at Chongqing; the Righteous Army Marshal Yang Han answered the call and arrived, wishing to kill him and absorb his army, but could not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Yuan Right Chancellor Wanerdu was recruiting troops at Chongqing. The Righteous Army Marshal Yang Han answered the summons, tried to kill Wanerdu and absorb his force, and failed.

sentences.zh: 漢走出峽，遇玉珍為言：「重慶無重兵，完者都與右丞哈麻禿不相能，若回船出不意襲之，可取而有也。

translations.literal: Han fled out of the gorge, met Yuzhen, and told him: "Chongqing has no heavy garrison; Wanerdu and the Right Chancellor Qimaya are at odds with each other — if you turn your ships back and strike unexpectedly, you can take and hold it."
translations.idiomatic: Han fled out of the gorge, met Yuzhen, and told him: "Chongqing has no strong garrison. Wanerdu and the Right Chancellor Qimaya are at odds. If you turn your fleet and strike by surprise, you can take the city."

sentences.zh: 」玉珍意未決，部將戴壽曰：「機不可失也。

translations.literal: Yuzhen had not yet decided; his subordinate general Dai Shou said: "This opportunity must not be lost."
translations.idiomatic: Yuzhen hesitated. His subordinate general Dai Shou said, "This chance must not be missed."

sentences.zh: 可分船為二，半貯糧歸沔陽，半因漢兵攻重慶，不濟則掠財物而還。

translations.literal: The ships can be divided in two: half store grain and return to Mianyang; half join Han's troops to attack Chongqing — if it fails, plunder goods and return.
translations.idiomatic: Split the fleet in two: half can store the grain and return to Mianyang, while half joins Han's men to attack Chongqing. If the attack fails, plunder what you can and withdraw."

sentences.zh: 」玉珍從其策，襲重慶，走完者都，執哈麻禿獻壽輝。

translations.literal: Yuzhen followed this plan, raided Chongqing, put Wanerdu to flight, seized Qimaya, and presented him to Shouhui.
translations.idiomatic: Yuzhen took his advice, raided Chongqing, put Wanerdu to flight, seized Qimaya, and sent him to Shouhui as a captive.

sentences.zh: 壽輝授玉珍隴蜀行省右丞。

translations.literal: Shouhui appointed Yuzhen Right Vice Minister of the Long-Shu Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Shouhui appointed Yuzhen Right Vice Minister of the Long-Shu Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 至正十七年也。

translations.literal: This was the seventeenth year of Zhizheng.
translations.idiomatic: This was the seventeenth year of Zhizheng (1357).

sentences.zh: 已而完者都自果州來，會平章朗革歹、參政趙資，謀復重慶，屯嘉定之大佛寺，玉珍遣萬勝禦之。

translations.literal: Before long Wanerdu came from Guozhou, joined Branch Secretariat Minister Lang Gedai and Vice Minister Zhao Zi, plotted to recover Chongqing, and encamped at the Great Buddha Temple in Jiading; Yuzhen sent Wan Sheng to oppose them.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Wanerdu came from Guozhou, joined Branch Secretariat Minister Lang Gedai and Vice Minister Zhao Zi, and plotted to recover Chongqing. They encamped at the Great Buddha Temple in Jiading, and Yuzhen sent Wan Sheng to oppose them.

sentences.zh: 勝，黃陂人，有智勇，玉珍寵愛之，使從己姓，眾呼為明二，後乃復姓名。

translations.literal: Sheng was a man of Huangpi, intelligent and brave; Yuzhen favored him, had him take his surname, and the people called him Ming the Second; later he restored his original name.
translations.idiomatic: Wan Sheng was a native of Huangpi, a man of wit and courage whom Yuzhen favored. Yuzhen had him take the Ming surname, and people called him Ming the Second; later he restored his original name.

sentences.zh: 勝攻嘉定，半年不下。

translations.literal: Sheng attacked Jiading but could not take it for half a year.
translations.idiomatic: Wan Sheng besieged Jiading but could not take it for half a year.

sentences.zh: 玉珍帥眾圍之，遣勝以輕兵襲陷成都，虜朗革歹及資妻子。

translations.literal: Yuzhen led the army to besiege it and sent Sheng with light troops in a surprise raid to capture Chengdu, taking Lang Gedai and Zi's wives and children prisoner.
translations.idiomatic: Yuzhen led the main force to besiege Jiading and sent Wan Sheng with light troops in a surprise raid that captured Chengdu, taking Lang Gedai and Zhao Zi's wives and children prisoner.

sentences.zh: 朗革歹妻自沉于江。

translations.literal: Lang Gedai's wife drowned herself in the river.
translations.idiomatic: Lang Gedai's wife drowned herself in the river.

sentences.zh: 以資妻子徇嘉定，招資降。

translations.literal: Using Zi's wife and children to display before Jiading, they summoned Zi to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: They paraded Zhao Zi's wife and children before Jiading to induce him to surrender.

sentences.zh: 資引弓射殺妻。

translations.literal: Zi drew his bow and shot his wife dead.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Zi drew his bow and shot his wife dead.

sentences.zh: 俄城破，執資及完者都、朗革歹歸於重慶，館諸治平寺，欲使為己用。

translations.literal: Before long the city fell; they seized Zi as well as Wanerdu and Lang Gedai and brought them to Chongqing, lodged them at Zhiping Temple, and wished to employ them for his own use.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the city fell. Zhao Zi, Wanerdu, and Lang Gedai were captured and taken to Chongqing, lodged at Zhiping Temple, where Yuzhen hoped to win them to his service.

sentences.zh: 三人者執不可，乃斬於市，以禮葬之，蜀人謂之「三忠」。

translations.literal: The three men obstinately refused; he then executed them in the market, buried them with ceremony, and the people of Shu called them the "Three Loyal Ones."
translations.idiomatic: All three steadfastly refused. They were executed in the marketplace and buried with full rites, and the people of Shu called them the "Three Loyal Ones."

sentences.zh: 於是諸郡縣相次來附。

translations.literal: Thereupon the various prefectures and counties submitted one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon prefecture after prefecture and county after county came over to him in succession.

sentences.zh: 二十年，陳友諒弑徐壽輝自立。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, Chen Youliang murdered Xu Shouhui and declared himself ruler.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year Chen Youliang murdered Xu Shouhui and proclaimed himself ruler.

sentences.zh: 玉珍曰：「與友諒俱臣徐氏，顧悖逆如此。

translations.literal: Yuzhen said: "Youliang and I were both subjects of the Xu clan—yet he turns so rebellious and perverse."
translations.idiomatic: Yuzhen said, "Youliang and I alike served the Xu house—yet he has turned so treacherous and rebellious."

sentences.zh: 」命以兵塞瞿塘，絕不與通。

translations.literal: He ordered troops to block Qutang and cut off all communication with him.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered troops to block Qutang Gorge and sever all ties with Youliang.

sentences.zh: 立壽輝廟于城南隅，歲時致祀。

translations.literal: He established a temple to Shouhui at the southeast corner of the city and offered sacrifices at the proper seasons.
translations.idiomatic: He erected a temple to Xu Shouhui in the city's southern quarter and offered seasonal sacrifices there.

sentences.zh: 自立為隴蜀王，以劉楨為參謀。

translations.literal: He declared himself Prince of Long-Shu and made Liu Zhen his strategic adviser.
translations.idiomatic: He declared himself Prince of Long-Shu and appointed Liu Zhen as his chief adviser.

sentences.zh: 楨，字維周，瀘州人。

translations.literal: Zhen, styled Weizhou, was a native of Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhen, styled Weizhou, was a native of Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 元進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi degree-holder of the Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: He had passed the Yuan dynasty jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 嘗為大名路經歷，棄官家居。

translations.literal: He had once served as an intendant of the Daming Circuit, then abandoned office and lived at home.
translations.idiomatic: He had once served as intendant of the Daming Circuit, then resigned and lived in retirement.

sentences.zh: 玉珍之攻重慶也，道瀘，部將劉澤民薦之。

translations.literal: When Yuzhen was attacking Chongqing, passing through Lu, his subordinate general Liu Zemin recommended him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuzhen was advancing on Chongqing, his route took him through Luzhou, where his officer Liu Zemin recommended Liu Zhen to him.

sentences.zh: 玉珍往見，與語大悅，即日延至舟中，尊禮備至。

translations.literal: Yuzhen went to see him, was greatly pleased in conversation, that same day invited him aboard his boat, and honored him with every courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Yuzhen went to meet him, was delighted by their conversation, invited him aboard his boat that very day, and received him with every mark of honor.

sentences.zh: 次年，楨屏人說曰：「西蜀形勝地，大王撫而有之，休養傷殘，用賢治兵，可以立不世業。

translations.literal: The next year, Zhen dismissed attendants and said: "Western Shu is a land of strategic strength. If the Great King pacifies and holds it, rests the wounded and disabled, employs the worthy and drills the troops, he can establish an achievement unmatched in the age.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Liu Zhen dismissed the attendants and said, "Western Shu is a land of natural strength. If Your Majesty settles and holds it, restores the war-worn and wounded, appoints worthy men and trains the army, you may found an achievement that will last for ages.

sentences.zh: 不於此時稱大號以系人心，一旦將士思鄉土，瓦解星散，大王孰與建國乎。

translations.literal: If you do not at this time assume a grand title to bind men's hearts, once officers and soldiers long for their native lands they will crumble and scatter like stars—how then, Great King, will you found a state?"
translations.idiomatic: If you do not proclaim a sovereign title now to bind men's hearts, the day your soldiers yearn for home the host will break apart and scatter—and then, Your Majesty, what state will you have left to build?"

sentences.zh: 」玉珍善之，乃謀於眾，以二十二年春僭即皇帝位於重慶，國號夏，建元天統。

translations.literal: Yuzhen approved this, consulted the assembly, and in the spring of the twenty-second year presumptuously ascended the imperial throne at Chongqing, with the state name Xia and the era name Tiantong.
translations.idiomatic: Yuzhen approved the plan. After consulting his followers, in the spring of the twenty-second year he presumptuously took the imperial throne at Chongqing, declaring the state Xia and adopting the era name Tiantong.

sentences.zh: 立妻彭氏為皇后，子升為太子。

translations.literal: He installed his wife Lady Peng as empress and his son Sheng as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: He made his wife Lady Peng empress and his son Sheng crown prince.

sentences.zh: 效周制，設六卿，以劉楨為宗伯。

translations.literal: Following the Zhou system, he established the Six Ministers and made Liu Zhen Minister of Ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Modeling his government on the Zhou, he established the Six Ministers and appointed Liu Zhen Minister of Ritual.

sentences.zh: 分蜀地為八道，更置府州縣官名。

translations.literal: He divided Shu territory into eight circuits and reorganized the names of prefecture, department, and county offices.
translations.idiomatic: He divided Shu into eight administrative circuits and reorganized the designations of prefectural, departmental, and county offices.

sentences.zh: 蜀兵視諸國為弱，勝兵不滿萬人。

translations.literal: Among the various states Shu troops were regarded as weak; battle-ready soldiers numbered fewer than ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Among the rival realms the Xia army was counted the weakest; effective fighting strength numbered fewer than ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 玉珍素無遠略，然性節儉，頗好學，折節下士。

translations.literal: Yuzhen by nature lacked far-reaching strategy, yet he was frugal by disposition, fond of learning, and humble toward scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Yuzhen had never possessed great strategic vision, yet he was frugal by nature, fond of study, and willing to humble himself before men of talent.

sentences.zh: 既即位，設國子監，教公卿子弟，設提舉司教授，建社稷宗廟，求雅樂，開進士科，定賦稅，以十分取一。

translations.literal: Once enthroned, he established the Directorate of Education to instruct the sons of officials, set up commissioners for instruction, built altars to soil and grain and ancestral temples, sought ceremonial music, opened the jinshi examination, and fixed taxation at one part in ten.
translations.idiomatic: Once enthroned, he established the Directorate of Education for the sons of the high nobility, appointed instructional commissioners, built the altars of state and ancestral temples, sought proper ceremonial music, restored the jinshi examination, and fixed the land tax at one-tenth.

sentences.zh: 蜀人悉便安之。

translations.literal: The people of Shu all found this convenient and settled.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Shu found all of this agreeable and settled contentedly under his rule.

sentences.zh: 皆劉楨為之謀也。

translations.literal: All of this was Liu Zhen's planning.
translations.idiomatic: All of this was Liu Zhen's counsel.

sentences.zh: 明年，遣萬勝由界首，鄒興由建昌，又指揮李某者由八番，分道攻雲南。

translations.literal: The next year he sent Wan Sheng by Jieshou, Zou Xing by Jianchang, and also a Commander Li by way of the Eight Fan territories, each by a separate route to attack Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he sent Wan Sheng via Jieshou, Zou Xing via Jianchang, and a certain Commander Li via the eight Fan territories, each by a separate route against Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 兩路皆不至，惟勝兵深入，元梁王走營金馬山。

translations.literal: Two routes never arrived; only Sheng's troops penetrated deep, and the Yuan Prince of Liang fled to encamp at Jinma Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Two of the columns never arrived. Only Wan Sheng's force pressed deep into enemy country, driving the Yuan Prince of Liang to take refuge on Jinma Mountain.

sentences.zh: 逾年，王挾大理兵擊勝，勝以孤軍無繼引還。

translations.literal: After a year the prince, with Dali troops, struck Sheng; Sheng, an isolated army without reinforcements, withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: A year later the prince struck back with Dali troops. Wan Sheng, unsupported and alone, withdrew.

sentences.zh: 復遣興取巴州。

translations.literal: He again sent Xing to take Bazhou.
translations.idiomatic: He again sent Zou Xing to capture Bazhou.

sentences.zh: 久之，復更六卿為中書省樞密院，改塚宰戴壽、司馬萬勝為左、右丞相，司寇向大亨、司空張文炳知樞密院事，司徒鄒興鎮成都，吳友仁鎮保甯，司寇莫仁壽鎮夔關，皆平章事。

translations.literal: After some time, he again replaced the Six Ministers with a Secretariat and Bureau of Military Affairs, changed Chief Minister Dai Shou and Minister of War Wan Sheng to Left and Right Chancellors, made Minister of Justice Xiang Daheng and Minister of Works Zhang Wenbing directors of the Bureau of Military Affairs, posted Minister of Education Zou Xing at Chengdu and Wu Youren at Baoning, made Minister of Justice Mo Renshou guardian of Kuiguan—all as Branch Secretariat ministers.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he reorganized the Six Ministers into a Secretariat and Bureau of Military Affairs, appointing Dai Shou and Wan Sheng Left and Right Chancellors, Xiang Daheng and Zhang Wenbing overseers of military affairs, Zou Xing as garrison commander at Chengdu, Wu Youren at Baoning, and Mo Renshou at Kuiguan—all with the rank of Branch Secretariat minister.

sentences.zh: 是歲，遣勝取興元，使參政江儼通好于太祖。

translations.literal: That year he sent Sheng to take Xingyuan and dispatched Vice Minister Jiang Yan to establish friendly relations with the Founding Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: That year he sent Wan Sheng to take Xingyuan and dispatched Vice Minister Jiang Yan to open friendly relations with the Founding Emperor.

sentences.zh: 太祖遣都事孫養浩報聘，遺玉珍書曰：「足下處西蜀，予處江左，蓋與漢季孫、劉相類。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor sent Chief Clerk Sun Yanghao in return and sent Yuzhen a letter saying: "You hold western Shu and I hold the lower Yangzi—much like Sun and Liu at the end of Han.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor sent Chief Clerk Sun Yanghao on a return mission and wrote to Yuzhen: "You hold western Shu and I the lower Yangzi region—we are much like Sun Quan and Liu Bei at the end of the Han.

sentences.zh: 近者王保保以鐵騎勁兵，虎踞中原，其志殆不在曹操下，使有謀臣如攸、彧，猛將如遼、郃，予兩人能高枕無憂乎。

translations.literal: Of late Wang Baobao with iron cavalry and strong troops crouches like a tiger over the Central Plain; his ambition is scarcely beneath Cao Cao's. If he had strategists like Xun You and Xun Yu and fierce generals like Zhang Liao and Zhang He—could the two of us rest our heads on high pillows without worry?
translations.idiomatic: Of late Wang Baobao has held the Central Plain with armored horse and hardened troops, tiger-like and immovable; his ambition is scarcely less than Cao Cao's. Were he served by advisers like Xun You and Xun Yu and captains like Zhang Liao and Zhang He—could you and I truly sleep without fear?

sentences.zh: 予與足下實脣齒邦，願以孫劉相吞噬為鑒。

translations.literal: You and I are truly states lip and teeth; I pray you take Sun and Liu devouring each other as a warning."
translations.idiomatic: Your realm and mine are lip and teeth to each other. Let us take warning from how Sun and Liu destroyed one another."

sentences.zh: 」自後信使往返不絕。

translations.literal: Thereafter envoys traveled back and forth without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter diplomatic messengers passed between them without interruption.

sentences.zh: 二十六年春，玉珍病革，召壽等諭曰：「西蜀險固，若協力同心，左右嗣子，則可以自守。

translations.literal: In the spring of the twenty-sixth year Yuzhen's illness turned critical; he summoned Shou and the others and instructed them: "Western Shu is steep and strong; if you join in strength and single heart to support the heir, you can hold it yourselves.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the twenty-sixth year, as Yuzhen lay dying, he summoned Dai Shou and the others and said, "Western Shu is rugged and easily defended. If you work together in loyalty and stand by my heir, you may yet hold the realm.

sentences.zh: 不然，後事非所知也。

translations.literal: Otherwise, what comes after is not for me to know."
translations.idiomatic: If not, I cannot foretell what will become of you."

sentences.zh: 」遂卒。

translations.literal: Thereupon he died.
translations.idiomatic: With that he died.

sentences.zh: 凡立五年，年三十六。

translations.literal: In all he had ruled five years; he was thirty-six years of age.
translations.idiomatic: He had reigned five years in all and was thirty-six at his death.

sentences.zh: 子升嗣，改元開熙，葬玉珍於江水之北，號永昌陵，廟號太祖。

translations.literal: His son Sheng succeeded, changed the era name to Kaixi, buried Yuzhen north of the river, naming the tomb Yongchang Mausoleum and the temple name Founding Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng succeeded him, changed the era name to Kaixi, and buried Yuzhen on the north bank of the Yangzi in the Yongchang Mausoleum, giving him the posthumous temple name Founding Emperor.

sentences.zh: 尊母彭氏為皇太后，同聽政。

translations.literal: He honored his mother Lady Peng as empress dowager and shared governance with her.
translations.idiomatic: He honored his mother Lady Peng as empress dowager, and mother and son ruled together.

sentences.zh: 升甫十歲，諸大臣皆粗暴，不肯相下。

translations.literal: Sheng had just turned ten; the chief ministers were all rough and overbearing, unwilling to yield to one another.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng was barely ten years old. The senior ministers were all coarse and domineering, and none would defer to the others.

sentences.zh: 而萬勝與張文炳有隙，勝密遣人殺之。

translations.literal: Wan Sheng and Zhang Wenbing had a rift; Sheng secretly sent men to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Wan Sheng and Zhang Wenbing bore a grudge against each other, and Wan Sheng secretly sent assassins to kill Zhang.

sentences.zh: 文炳所善玉珍養子明昭，復矯彭氏旨縊殺勝。

translations.literal: Ming Zhao, Yuzhen's adopted son whom Wenbing had favored, again forged an order in Lady Peng's name and had Sheng strangled.
translations.idiomatic: Ming Zhao, Yuzhen's adopted son and Zhang Wenbing's ally, then forged an order in the empress dowager's name and had Wan Sheng strangled.

sentences.zh: 勝於明氏功最多，其死，蜀人多憐之。

translations.literal: Sheng's service to the Ming house had been greatest; at his death many in Shu pitied him.
translations.idiomatic: Wan Sheng had done more for the Ming house than any other man. At his death the people of Shu mourned him widely.

sentences.zh: 吳友仁自保寧移檄，以清君側為名。

translations.literal: Wu Youren issued a proclamation from Baoning under the banner of clearing evil counsel from the ruler's side.
translations.idiomatic: From Baoning Wu Youren issued a proclamation in the name of purging evil counselors from the ruler's side.

sentences.zh: 升命戴壽討之。

translations.literal: Sheng ordered Dai Shou to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng ordered Dai Shou to march against him.

sentences.zh: 友仁遺壽書謂：「不誅昭，則國必不安，眾必不服。

translations.literal: Youren sent Shou a letter saying: "If Zhao is not executed, the state cannot be secure and the host will not submit.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Youren wrote to Dai Shou: "Unless Zhao is put to death, the realm will know no peace and the army will not obey.

sentences.zh: 昭朝誅，吾當夕至。

translations.literal: If Zhao is executed this morning, I shall arrive by evening."
translations.idiomatic: Execute Zhao at dawn and I shall reach the capital by nightfall."

sentences.zh: 」壽乃奏誅昭，友仁入朝謝罪。

translations.literal: Shou then memorialized for Zhao's execution; Youren entered court to beg forgiveness.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Shou memorialized for Zhao's execution. Wu Youren then came to court to confess his fault.

sentences.zh: 於是諸大臣用事，而友仁尤專恣，國柄旁落，遂益不振。

translations.literal: Thereupon the chief ministers wielded power, Youren especially arbitrary; state authority slipped aside and the realm grew ever weaker.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the great ministers held real power, Wu Youren above all overbearing and unrestrained. Authority slipped from the throne, and the state weakened further.

sentences.zh: 萬勝既死，劉楨為右丞相，後三年卒。

translations.literal: After Wan Sheng's death Liu Zhen became Right Chancellor; three years later he died.
translations.idiomatic: After Wan Sheng's death Liu Zhen became Right Chancellor; he died three years later.

sentences.zh: 是歲，升遣使告哀于太祖，已，又遣使入聘。

translations.literal: That year Sheng sent envoys to report mourning to the Founding Emperor; afterward he again sent envoys on a friendly mission.
translations.idiomatic: That year Sheng sent envoys to the Founding Emperor to announce his father's death, and afterward sent another mission to pay a courtesy visit.

sentences.zh: 太祖亦遣侍御史蔡哲報之。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor also sent Supervising Censor Cai Zhe in reply.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor sent Supervising Censor Cai Zhe in return.

sentences.zh: 洪武元年，太祖克元都，升奉書稱賀。

translations.literal: In the first year of Hongwu, when the Founding Emperor took the Yuan capital, Sheng sent a letter of congratulation.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 1, when the Founding Emperor captured the Yuan capital, Sheng sent a letter of congratulation.

sentences.zh: 明年，太祖遣使求大木。

translations.literal: The next year the Founding Emperor sent envoys to request large timber.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the Founding Emperor sent envoys requesting large timber.

sentences.zh: 升遂並獻方物。

translations.literal: Sheng thereupon also presented local products.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng also sent tribute goods of the region.

sentences.zh: 帝答以璽書。

translations.literal: The Emperor replied with an imperial sealed letter.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor answered with an edict under the imperial seal.

sentences.zh: 其冬，遣平章楊璟諭升歸命。

translations.literal: That winter he dispatched Branch Secretariat Minister Yang Jing to instruct Sheng to submit.
translations.idiomatic: That winter the court sent Branch Secretariat Minister Yang Jing to urge Sheng to surrender.

sentences.zh: 升不從。

translations.literal: Sheng would not comply.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng refused.

sentences.zh: 璟復遺升書曰：

translations.literal: Jing again sent Sheng a letter saying:
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jing wrote again to Sheng:

sentences.zh: 古之為國者，同力度德，同德度義，，故能身家兩全，流譽無窮，反是者輒敗。

translations.literal: Those of old who founded states—matching strength then measuring virtue, matching virtue then measuring righteousness,, therefore could preserve body and house both complete, fame flowing without end; those contrary to this always failed.
translations.idiomatic: The founders of states in antiquity weighed their strength against their rivals' and their virtue against their rivals'; so they preserved both their lives and their houses and won everlasting renown. Those who did otherwise were invariably destroyed.

sentences.zh: 足下幼沖，席先人業，據有巴、蜀，不咨至計，而聽群下之議，以瞿塘、劍閣之險，一夫負戈，萬人無如之何。

translations.literal: You, young and tender, inheriting your forebear's enterprise, holding Ba and Shu, do not consult supreme plans but heed subordinates' talk—that with Qutang and Jiange's peril, one man bearing arms, ten thousand men can do nothing against him.
translations.idiomatic: You are young and have inherited your father's realm in Ba and Shu, yet you do not seek counsel on the course that matters most. Instead you heed the chatter of your subordinates, who tell you that Qutang and Jiange are impregnable—that a single man with a spear can hold off ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 此皆不達時變以誤足下之言也。

translations.literal: These are all words that fail to grasp changing times and mislead you.
translations.idiomatic: Such talk shows no grasp of how the times have changed—it can only lead you astray.

sentences.zh: 昔據蜀最盛者，莫如漢昭烈。

translations.literal: Of old those who held Shu at greatest strength, none matched Han's Zhao Lie.
translations.idiomatic: In past ages no ruler of Shu ever stood stronger than Emperor Zhao Lie of Han.

sentences.zh: 且以諸葛武侯佐之，綜核官守，訓練士卒，財用不足，皆取之南詔。

translations.literal: Moreover with Chancellor Zhuge assisting him, auditing official posts, drilling soldiers—when funds fell short, all was taken from Nanzhao.
translations.idiomatic: And he had Chancellor Zhuge Liang at his side, tightening the administration, drilling the troops, and drawing whatever funds he lacked from Nanzhao.

sentences.zh: 然猶朝不謀夕，僅能自保。

translations.literal: Yet still he did not plan from morning to evening—barely able to preserve himself.
translations.idiomatic: Even so he lived from one day to the next and barely managed to hold his ground.

sentences.zh: 今足下疆場，南不過播州，北不過漢中，以此准彼，相去萬萬，而欲藉一隅之地，延命頃刻，可謂智乎？

translations.literal: Now your borders—south not beyond Bozhou, north not beyond Hanzhong—using this to measure against that, the distance is ten thousand ten thousands; yet you wish to rely on a corner of land to prolong life a moment—can this be called wisdom?
translations.idiomatic: Your borders today reach no farther south than Bozhou and no farther north than Hanzhong. Compare that to Liu Bei's realm and the gap is beyond reckoning. Yet you would stake your life on a corner of the map and buy yourself a few breaths more—is that wisdom?

sentences.zh: 我主上仁聖威武，神明回應，順附者無不加恩，負固者然後致討。

translations.literal: Our sovereign is benevolent, sage, martial, and awesome; spirits respond; those who submit receive overflowing favor; only those who stubbornly resist then face chastisement.
translations.idiomatic: Our sovereign is humane and sagely, martial and awesome, aided by Heaven's response. All who yield receive boundless grace; only the stubborn are punished.

sentences.zh: 以足下先人通好之故，不忍加師，數使使諭意。

translations.literal: Because of friendly relations with your forebear, he cannot bear to send armies; repeatedly he sends envoys to declare his intent.
translations.idiomatic: Out of friendship for your late father he has been unwilling to march against you and has sent envoy after envoy to make his intent plain.

sentences.zh: 又以足下年幼，未曆事變，恐惑於狂瞽，失遠大計，故復遣璟面諭禍福。

translations.literal: Also because you are young, have not passed through shifts of affairs, fearing confusion by mad blind men and loss of far-reaching plans, therefore again dispatching Jing in person to explain fortune and ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing that you are young and untested in affairs of state, and fearing that reckless counsel may lead you to abandon the larger design, he has now sent me in person to set fortune and ruin plainly before you.

sentences.zh: 深仁厚德，所以待明氏者不淺，足下可不深念乎？

translations.literal: Deep benevolence and thick virtue—the manner of treating the Ming house is not shallow; can you not deeply reflect?
translations.idiomatic: Such depth of kindness and magnanimity in his dealings with the Ming house is no small thing. Can you not weigh it carefully?

sentences.zh: 且向者如陳、張之屬，竊據吳、楚，造舟塞江河，積糧過山嶽，強將勁兵，自謂無敵。

translations.literal: Moreover formerly men like Chen and Zhang—seizing Wu and Chu, building boats to block rivers, piling grain surpassing mountains, strong generals and fierce troops, calling themselves without rival.
translations.idiomatic: Consider those who came before—Chen Youliang, Zhang Shicheng, and their like. They carved out Wu and Chu, built fleets that clogged the rivers, piled grain higher than the hills, and mustered champions and hardened troops, thinking themselves invincible.

sentences.zh: 然鄱陽一戰，友諒授首，旋師東討，張氏面縛。

translations.literal: Yet at one battle at Poyang, Youliang lost his head; wheeling the army east to strike, the Zhang clan came bound face to face.
translations.idiomatic: Yet at a single battle on Lake Poyang Youliang lost his life; the armies turned east, and Zhang Shicheng was brought in bonds.

sentences.zh: 此非人力，實天命也。

translations.literal: This is not human power—it is truly Heaven's mandate.
translations.idiomatic: That was not mere force of arms—it was the mandate of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 足下視此何如？

translations.literal: You—how do you view this?
translations.idiomatic: What lesson do you draw from this?

sentences.zh: 友諒子竄歸江夏，王師致伐，勢窮銜璧。

translations.literal: Youliang's son fled back to Jiangxia; the royal army arrived to punish; strength exhausted, he came bearing jade at his lips.
translations.idiomatic: Youliang's son fled to Jiangxia; when the imperial army marched against him, he was driven to utter desperation and came bearing jade in submission.

sentences.zh: 主上宥其罪愆，剖符錫爵，恩榮之盛，天下所知。

translations.literal: Our sovereign pardoned his crimes, carved tally and bestowed rank—the splendor of grace and honor, all under Heaven knows.
translations.idiomatic: Our sovereign pardoned his offenses, granted him a fief and noble rank—a generosity famed throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 足下無彼之過，而能翻然覺悟，自求多福，則必享茅土之封，保先人之祀，世世不絕，豈不賢智矣哉？

translations.literal: You lack his faults, yet if you can suddenly awaken, seek much fortune for yourself, then must enjoy feudal seal of thatched earth, preserve your forebear's sacrifices, generation after generation unbroken—is this not wise and worthy?
translations.idiomatic: You have committed no such crimes. If you can turn at once and choose the path of blessing, you will surely receive a noble fief, preserve your father's sacrifices for generations to come, and win praise as a man of sense and virtue—is that not the better course?

sentences.zh: 若必欲崛強一隅，假息頃刻，魚遊沸鼎，燕巢危幕，禍害將至，恬不自知。

translations.literal: If you must wish to rise stubborn in one corner, borrow breath a moment—fish swimming in boiling cauldron, swallows nesting on perilous curtain—calamity about to arrive, serene without knowing yourself.
translations.idiomatic: If you insist on clinging defiantly to a single corner and buying a few moments' respite, you are a fish swimming in a boiling pot, a swallow nesting beneath a tottering eave—disaster is near, yet you do not see it.

sentences.zh: 璟恐天兵一臨，凡今為足下謀者，他日或各自為身計，以取富貴。

translations.literal: Jing fears when Heaven's armies once arrive, all who now plan for you—in days to come may each scheme for himself to obtain wealth and honor.
translations.idiomatic: I fear that when the imperial armies arrive, those who counsel you today may each look to his own safety and sell you out for rank and riches.

sentences.zh: 當此之時，老母弱子，將安所歸？

translations.literal: At such a time, old mother and weak son—where will they go?
translations.idiomatic: When that day comes, your aged mother and helpless child—where will they find refuge?

sentences.zh: 禍福利害，瞭然可睹，在足下審之而已。

translations.literal: Fortune and ruin, benefit and harm—clearly visible; it rests with you to examine—that is all.
translations.idiomatic: Blessing and ruin lie plain before you. The choice is yours alone to make.

sentences.zh: 升終不聽。

translations.literal: Sheng in the end would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng refused to heed him to the end.

sentences.zh: 又明年，興元守將以城降。

translations.literal: The next year again, the Xingyuan garrison commander surrendered the city.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the garrison commander of Xingyuan surrendered the city.

sentences.zh: 吳友仁數往攻之，不克。

translations.literal: Wu Youren several times went to attack but could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Youren attacked repeatedly but could not recover it.

sentences.zh: 是歲，太祖遣使假道征雲南，升不奉詔。

translations.literal: That year the Founding Emperor sent envoys requesting passage to campaign against Yunnan; Sheng did not obey the edict.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Founding Emperor sent envoys requesting passage through Xia territory to campaign against Yunnan; Sheng refused the order.

sentences.zh: 四年正月命征西將軍湯和帥副將軍廖永忠等以舟師由瞿塘趨重慶，前將軍傅友德帥副將軍顧時等以步騎由秦、隴趨成都，伐蜀。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year he ordered Campaign General of the West Tang He leading Deputy Generals Liao Yongzhong and others with river forces by Qutang toward Chongqing, and Forward General Fu Youde leading Deputy Generals Gu Shi and others with infantry and cavalry by Qin and Long toward Chengdu, to attack Shu.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fourth year he ordered Tang He, Campaign General of the West, to lead Deputy Generals Liao Yongzhong and others with the fleet up the Qutang route toward Chongqing, and Fu Youde, Forward General, to lead Deputy Generals Gu Shi and others with infantry and cavalry through Qin and Long toward Chengdu—the two-pronged invasion of Shu.

sentences.zh: 初，壽言於升曰：「以王保保、李思齊之強，猶莫能與明抗，況吾蜀乎！

translations.literal: Initially Shou said to Sheng: "With Wang Baobao and Li Siqi's strength, still none could resist Ming—how much less our Shu!
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Dai Shou had said to Sheng, "Men as powerful as Wang Baobao and Li Siqi could not stand against Ming—how much less can we in Shu!

sentences.zh: 一旦有警，計安出？

translations.literal: Once there is alarm, what plan will you produce?"
translations.idiomatic: If war comes, what plan do we have?"

sentences.zh: 」友仁曰：「不然，吾蜀襟山帶江，非中原比，莫若外交好而內修備。

translations.literal: Youren said: "Not so—our Shu embraces mountains and girds rivers, not comparable to the Central Plain; nothing better than outward friendship and inward preparedness.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Youren said, "Not so. Shu is girded by mountains and rivers—not comparable to the open Central Plain. Our best course is friendship abroad and readiness at home.

sentences.zh: 」升以為然，遣莫仁壽以鐵索橫斷瞿塘峽口。

translations.literal: Sheng thought this right and sent Mo Renshou to stretch iron chains across Qutang Gorge mouth.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng agreed and sent Mo Renshou to block the mouth of Qutang Gorge with iron chains stretched across the river.

sentences.zh: 至是又遣壽、友仁、鄒興等益兵為助。

translations.literal: At this time he again sent Shou, Youren, Zou Xing and others with added troops as reinforcement.
translations.idiomatic: When the invasion came he sent Dai Shou, Wu Youren, Zou Xing, and others with reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 北倚羊角山，南倚南城砦，鑿兩岸石壁，引鐵索為飛橋，用木板置礮以拒敵。

translations.literal: North relying on Yangjiao Mountain, south relying on Nancheng Stockade, carving both banks' stone cliffs, drawing iron chains as flying bridge, using wooden boards to set catapults to repel the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: They fortified the north at Yangjiao Mountain and the south at Nancheng Stockade, cut into the cliff faces on both banks, stretched iron chains to form a flying bridge, and mounted catapults on wooden platforms to repel the enemy.

sentences.zh: 和軍至，不能進。

translations.literal: He's army arrived but could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Tang He's army arrived but could advance no farther.

sentences.zh: 傅友德覘階、文無備，進破之，又破綿州。

translations.literal: Fu Youde observed Jie and Wen undefended, advanced and broke them, then also broke Mianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Youde found Jiezhou and Wenzhou undefended, stormed them, and went on to take Mianzhou.

sentences.zh: 壽乃留興等守瞿塘，而自與友仁還，會向大亨之師以援漢州。

translations.literal: Shou then left Xing and others to guard Qutang, while he himself with Youren returned to join Xiang Daheng's army to aid Hanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Shou left Zou Xing and others to hold Qutang and marched back with Wu Youren to join Xiang Daheng's force in relief of Hanzhou.

sentences.zh: 數戰皆大敗，壽、大亨走成都，友仁走保寧。

translations.literal: Several battles all greatly defeated; Shou and Daheng fled to Chengdu, Youren fled to Baoning.
translations.idiomatic: They fought several engagements and were routed each time. Dai Shou and Xiang Daheng fled to Chengdu; Wu Youren fled to Baoning.

sentences.zh: 時永忠亦破瞿塘關。

translations.literal: At the same time Yongzhong also broke Qutang Pass.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time Liao Yongzhong broke through Qutang Pass.

sentences.zh: 飛橋鐵索皆燒斷，興中矢死，夏兵皆潰。

translations.literal: The flying bridges and iron chains were all burned through; Xing was struck by an arrow and died, and the Xia troops all collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: The pontoon bridges and iron chains were burned away; Xing was killed by an arrow, and the Xia army broke in rout.

sentences.zh: 遂下夔州，師次銅羅峽。

translations.literal: Thereupon they took Kuizhou, and the army halted at Tongluo Gorge.
translations.idiomatic: They then seized Kuizhou and encamped at Tongluo Gorge.

sentences.zh: 升大懼，右丞劉仁勸奔成都。

translations.literal: Sheng was greatly afraid; the Right Chancellor Liu Ren urged him to flee to Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng was terrified, and his Right Chancellor Liu Ren urged him to flee to Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 升母彭泣曰：「成都可到，亦僅延旦夕命。

translations.literal: Sheng's mother Peng wept and said: "Chengdu may be reached, but it would only prolong life for a morning and an evening."
translations.idiomatic: Sheng's mother Lady Peng wept and said, "We might reach Chengdu, but that would only buy us another day or two of life."

sentences.zh: 大軍所過，勢如破竹，不如早降以活民命。

translations.literal: Where the great army passes, its momentum is like splitting bamboo — better to surrender early and preserve the people's lives.
translations.idiomatic: Where the Ming army advances, resistance crumbles like bamboo under a blade. Better to surrender now and spare the people.

sentences.zh: 」於是遣使齎表乞降。

translations.literal: Thereupon he sent envoys bearing a memorial to beg surrender.
translations.idiomatic: She then sent envoys with a formal surrender petition.

sentences.zh: 升面縛銜璧輿櫬，與母彭及官屬降於軍門。

translations.literal: Sheng, with face bound and jade disk in his mouth, came in the funeral carriage, and with his mother Peng and the officials surrendered at the army gate.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng came bound, the jade surrender disk in his mouth, riding in the funeral cart, and with his mother Lady Peng and his officials surrendered at the camp gate.

sentences.zh: 和受璧，永忠解縛，承旨撫慰，下令諸將不得有所侵擾。

translations.literal: He accepted the jade disk; Yongzhong untied the bonds; as ordered he comforted them and commanded the generals not to commit any harassment.
translations.idiomatic: Tang He accepted the jade disk; Liao Yongzhong cut his bonds; by imperial order they were reassured, and the generals were forbidden to plunder or harass.

sentences.zh: 而壽、大亨亦以成都降于友德。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Shou and Daheng also surrendered Chengdu to Youde.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Shou and Daheng also surrendered Chengdu to Fu Youde.

sentences.zh: 升等悉送京師，禮臣奏言：「皇帝御奉天殿，明升等俯伏待罪午門外，有司宣制赦，如孟昶降宋故事。

translations.literal: Sheng and the others were all sent to the capital; the ritual officials memorialized: "The Emperor shall attend at Fengtian Hall; Ming Sheng and the others shall prostrate themselves awaiting judgment outside the Meridian Gate; the relevant offices shall proclaim the amnesty decree, following the precedent of Meng Chang's surrender to Song."
translations.idiomatic: Sheng and his party were sent to the capital.
