The ritual officials proposed: "Let the Emperor receive them in Fengtian Hall while Ming Sheng and his followers prostrate themselves outside the Meridian Gate awaiting judgment, with the appropriate offices proclaiming an amnesty decree, following the precedent of Meng Chang's surrender to Song."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「升幼弱，事由臣下，與孟昶異，宜免其伏地上表待罪之儀。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Sheng is young and weak; the affair was the work of his ministers, different from Meng Chang — he ought to be exempted from the rite of prostrating on the ground to present a memorial awaiting judgment."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "Sheng is young and weak, and his ministers drove events — unlike Meng Chang. He should be spared the rite of prostrating to present a memorial of guilt."

sentences.zh: 」是日授升爵歸義侯，賜第京師。

translations.literal: That same day Sheng was granted the title Marquis of Guiyi and given a residence in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: That same day Sheng was enfeoffed as Marquis of Guiyi and given a mansion in the capital.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，和等悉定川、蜀諸郡縣，執友仁于保寧，遂班師。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter, He and the others fully pacified the prefectures and counties of Sichuan, captured Youren at Baoning, and thereupon withdrew the army.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth winter month Tang He and his colleagues pacified the prefectures and counties of Sichuan, captured Youren at Baoning, and withdrew the army.

sentences.zh: 壽、大亨、仁壽皆鑿舟自沉死。

translations.literal: Shou, Daheng, and Renshou all scuttled their boats and drowned themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Shou, Daheng, and Renshou all scuttled their boats and drowned themselves.

sentences.zh: 丁世貞者，文州守將也，友德攻文州，據險力戰，汪興祖死焉。

translations.literal: Ding Shizhen was the defending general of Wenzhou; Youde attacked Wenzhou; he held the defiles and fought fiercely, and Wang Xingzu died there.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Shizhen was the defender of Wenzhou. When Fu Youde attacked the city, he held the passes and fought stubbornly; Wang Xingzu was killed in the battle.

sentences.zh: 文州破，遁去。

translations.literal: When Wenzhou fell, he fled.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenzhou fell, he escaped.

sentences.zh: 已復以兵破文州，殺硃顯忠，友德擊走之。

translations.literal: Before long he again led troops to break Wenzhou, killed Zhu Xianzhong, and Youde struck and drove him off.
translations.idiomatic: He soon returned, retook Wenzhou, and killed Zhu Xianzhong before Fu Youde drove him off again.

sentences.zh: 夏亡，復集余眾圍秦州五十日。

translations.literal: After Xia perished, he again gathered remnant forces and besieged Qinzhou for fifty days.
translations.idiomatic: After the fall of Xia he rallied remnant troops and besieged Qinzhou for fifty days.

sentences.zh: 兵敗，夜宿梓潼廟，為其下所殺。

translations.literal: His army was defeated; he lodged at night in the Zitong temple and was killed by his subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: Defeated in battle, he spent the night in the Zitong shrine and was killed by his own men.

sentences.zh: 友仁至京師，帝以其寇漢中，首造兵端，令明氏失國，僇於市。

translations.literal: Youren reached the capital; the Emperor, because he had raided Hanzhong and first raised the banner of war, causing the Ming house to lose its state, executed him in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: When Youren reached the capital, the Emperor had him executed in the marketplace for having raided Hanzhong, opened hostilities, and brought about the fall of the Ming house of Xia.

sentences.zh: 戍他將校於徐州。

translations.literal: His other officers and commanders were garrisoned at Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The other Xia officers were exiled to garrison duty at Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 明年徙升於高麗。

translations.literal: The next year Sheng was relocated to Goryeo.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Sheng was exiled to Goryeo.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：友諒、士誠起刀筆負販，因亂僭竊，恃其富強，而卒皆敗於其所恃。

translations.literal: The appraiser says: Youliang and Shicheng rose from clerk's work and peddling burdens; through disorder they usurped and stole power, relied on their wealth and strength, and in the end all were defeated by what they relied upon.
translations.idiomatic: The historian comments: Youliang and Shicheng rose from clerks and peddlers, seized power in the chaos, and trusted in their wealth and armies — yet in the end they were undone by the very strengths on which they relied.

sentences.zh: 跡其始終成敗之故，太祖料之審矣。

translations.literal: Tracing the causes of their rise and fall from beginning to end, the Founding Emperor judged them with precision.
translations.idiomatic: Tracing the causes of their rise and fall from first to last, one sees how precisely the Founding Emperor had read them.

sentences.zh: 國珍首亂，反覆無信，然竟獲良死，玉珍乘勢，割據一隅，僭號二世，皆不可謂非幸也。

translations.literal: Guozhen was first to raise disorder, fickle and faithless, yet in the end obtained a good death; Yuzhen rode the momentum, carved out a corner of the realm, and usurped an imperial title for two generations — all cannot be said to have lacked good fortune.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhen was the first to stir rebellion and proved faithless again and again, yet died a natural death; Yuzhen seized his moment, held a corner of the empire, and maintained a usurped throne for two generations — none of them can be said to have lacked luck.

sentences.zh: 國珍又名谷珍，蓋降後避明諱雲。

translations.literal: Guozhen was also called Guzhen, having after surrender avoided the Ming taboo on Yun.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhen was also known as Guzhen, having changed his name after surrender to observe the Ming taboo.
